content.content:
### 5b. C — Vision segmentation for a cached mask

Measured 2026-09-15 on the same host (macOS 26.5.1, M2 Max, 16-core Neural
Engine) by `vision_stills.swift` and `vision_job.swift`, fixtures by
`vision_fixtures.sh`, run from a shell under the terminal's attribution.
The machine was busy (load 5–60), so times are upper bounds (±1.3×).

1. **API.** Both requests are synchronous through `VNImageRequestHandler`
   (the newer Swift `perform(on:)` is `async`-only). One revision each, no
   required setting, **no TCC grant**. Person segmentation always returns ONE
   `VNPixelBufferObservation`, even with no person, at a size that ignores
   the input: fast 256×192, balanced 512×384, accurate 2016×1512 — always
   4:3 (portrait input gives the transposed sizes; a square input is
   inconsistent between qualities). Foreground returns zero or one
   `VNInstanceMaskObservation`, labels at 512×512. Every mask covers the
   whole frame in normalised coordinates, stretched, y down. Foreground
   cannot run on the CPU (`unsupported compute device`).
2. **Speed**, warm medians at 1080p: person fast 6.6 ms, balanced 28.3 ms,
   accurate 65.1 ms; foreground 18.0 ms for its 512² mask; 4K is within a
   few ms of 1080p. Cold first call 99–299 ms. The realistic job, a 60 s
   1080p30 H.264 decoded at 10 frames per second of source: decode alone
   21–25× realtime; **person balanced 4.2–5.5×**; foreground 5.4–7.0×;
   person fast 13.6–16.5×; accurate 1.6–1.7×; balanced on the CPU 0.7×.
3. **Determinism.** On ONE device, byte-identical: fresh against fresh in a
   process, 54 of 54 stills across two processes, 600 of 600 masks across two
   whole-job runs for balanced (ANE and CPU) and foreground. Across DEVICES,
   different: balanced up to 25 levels (GPU) and 11 (CPU), accurate up to
   32, foreground ANE against GPU up to 255 on 0.04–0.8 % of pixels. Auto
   equals ANE. **`.fast` is stateful**: a reused request or a sequence
   handler matched a fresh request on 5 of 600 masks (mean difference 46);
   balanced, accurate and foreground carry no state (600 of 600).
4. **No person.** Person segmentation on cards, text and Reelcut's own UI:
   0.00 % of pixels above 127, maxima 0–31, on every one of 600 masks of a
   scrolling-UI recording; a faint haze up to value 75 on a photo; a test
   pattern under accurate put 0.63 % above 127. **Foreground returns no
   observation at all** on cards, text, test patterns and the UI (900 of 900
   frames) and cuts anything salient otherwise — a circle, a sheet of paper,
   a monitor. A screen recording showing a film: both cut out the actors.
5. **Person content** (system-shipped images and road map 3's film
   recordings — no personal files): a frontal portrait 29.2–29.3 % in every
   mode; arms raised under dramatic light 3.9 % person (part of an arm)
   against 15.6 % foreground (the whole figure); a person from behind 0 %
   person against 39 % foreground; a small silhouette 0 % against 1.8 %.
   Quality on real camera footage — hair, motion blur — unmeasured.
6. **Cache.** Per mask raw: person balanced 196,608 B (112.5 MB per 60 s
   at 10/s), foreground 262,144 B. As PNG: balanced 12.4–32.9 KB (16.2 MB
   for the 60 s film job), foreground 4.6–7.2 KB (3.7 MB). Accurate raw is
   1.70 GiB per 60 s.
7. **Stability.** A static portrait at 30 fps: mean consecutive difference
   0.16 (balanced), 0.09 (accurate), 0.05 (foreground) levels. A static shot
   from behind under foreground: 5.3, 3.4 % of pixels flipping. **A slow
   push-in under foreground: coverage swinging 10–85 %, up to 57 % of pixels
   flipping between masks 0.1 s apart** — the monitor pops in and out.

**Could not measure:** the first-ever Neural Engine compile, masks across
machines or OS versions, real camera footage of a person, concurrent
requests, YUV input, TCC in the signed bundle, an idle host.

**Verdict: E9 is buildable as PERSON segmentation at `.balanced` for video,
with foreground for pictures only, a pinned device, and a per-window "no
subject" rule** — the plan's two-subject design for video was overturned by
q7, and q4 is why the rule exists.

### 5c. Questions left for build time, each a phase's first step

- **E3** — the tone group's per-pixel cost at the 8 ms budget with the fast
  path's flag; and the `kGatherFilters` register counts re-measured after the
  header move.
- **E4** — each new gather's tap cost; whether the specialization's dead-code
  cost crosses the budget (the fallback is a constant per gather class); and
  whether the spotlight lens can already carry obscured content out of a
  region (D7).
- **E5** — a two-texel gradient through a `rgba16Float` 3D texture with the
  linear sampler, before the looks are written.
- **E6** — none: the reviewer verified by reading that `DestinationPass.open()`
  resumes a suspended pass with `.load`, so framebuffer fetch sees every
  earlier layer and shadow.
- **E8** — the three unmeasured rows above.
- **E9** — the first-ever Neural Engine compile cost, and a mask-quality
  check on real camera footage by a person at the machine.
- Two reviewers read this plan against the tree before it was trusted (§10).

## 6. The phases
### E9 — Remove Background (D5)

**Adds:** cutting a person out of a picture without a green screen. Schema
**v15**. No op, no tool beyond a `set_video` key. Written against §5b.

**Schema.** `video.cutout`: `null` or `{subject: person | foreground,
feather 0–1}`.
- **`person`** — `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` at `.balanced`, a
  FRESH request per frame. Not `.fast`, which carries state from earlier
  frames (a reused request matched a fresh one on 5 of 600 masks), so a
  partial or random-access rebuild could never reproduce it; not
  `.accurate`, which runs at 1.7× realtime, stores 1.7 GiB per minute at
  native size and was no better on the portraits measured.
- **`foreground`** — `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest`, allowed on
  IMAGE and STILL sources only and refused by name on a media clip. On video
  it picks whatever is salient per frame — a monitor merging into the
  subject, up to 57 % of pixels flipping between masks 0.1 s apart on a slow
  push-in — which no cache can make steady; on a single picture it is the
  better request (the whole figure where person segmentation found part of
  an arm, or nothing, from behind).

**The analysis — `MediaImporter+Masks.swift`** (new):
- Requested by the first clip that asks, and only for the source windows
  clips with a cutout show (Concat's shape), at **10 masks per second of
  source**, written as 8-bit PNG at the request's native size (512×384 for
  `person`, 12–33 KB each — about 16 MB per minute on the film recording
  measured) under `cache/masks/<media id>-<subject>/`, with `CacheStamp`,
  the marker written last, the vouching rule of `thumbs/`, and the ledger.
  Decoding is `AVAssetReader` of the CODED buffer, so a mask is in the coded
  orientation.
- **Synchronous and grant-free**: the `VN*` classes' `perform` is
  synchronous (the newer Swift `perform(on:)` is `async`-only and is not
  used) and no TCC grant was requested. At ~5× realtime a minute of source
  takes ~12 s; an hour, ~12 min — a background pass with progress in the
  section, cancelled with the document.
- **The compute device is PINNED** (`setComputeDevice`, Neural Engine where
  present, else GPU) and written into the marker, because masks are
  byte-identical across processes on one device but differ across devices
  (up to 25 levels GPU against ANE on `.balanced`). **The marker never
  promises byte-identical REGENERATION**: a package opened on another Mac
  uses the masks it carries, and every proof compares a render against the
  CACHED mask, never against a recomputation.

**The "no subject" rule — the one that keeps a screencast.** Person
segmentation returns a mask for every frame, about zero on cards, text and
the app's own UI (0.00 % of pixels above 127 on all 600 masks of a
scrolling-UI recording), and foreground returns no observation at all.
Multiplied straight into alpha, that would erase a screencast. So the
decision is made per CLIP WINDOW, not per frame: when no mask in the window
has at least 0.5 % of its pixels above 127, the cutout draws NOTHING — the
clip renders uncut — and the section says "No person found". Per frame it
would flicker: a person leaving the shot would switch the background in and
out. Within a window that has a subject, every frame's mask is honoured, so
a person walking out of frame leaves an empty picture, which is what was
asked for. A screencast showing a film is cut down to the film's actors —
correct by the rule and surprising to a person; the section's note says
what was found.

**Metal.** The core emits `source_t` on a layer (it knows `in`, speed and
the reversed mirror); Swift binds the NEAREST mask as fragment `texture(2)`
(a 1×1 opaque placeholder; balanced masks move 0.16 levels per frame on a
static shot, so nearest-of-10-per-second does not visibly step, and a blend
of two would cost a third texture), sampled by NORMALISED coordinate — the
mask is 4:3 or square whatever the frame, stretched over it — at the SAME
coordinate as the picture: after the spotlight lens and pixelate snap, and
through `orientedUV(uv, quarterTurns, mirrored)` (`Compositor.metal:533-534`),
because the mask is built from the coded buffer. Feathered, and multiplied
into coverage at step 7 beside E3's mask, so shadow and reflection follow.
A frame whose mask is not computed yet draws UNCUT, never blank.
`partnerBox`'s guard adds cut-out partners (E3's list). Uniforms: a flag,
the feather and two spares, one group of four.

**UI.** A **Background** section beside Chroma Key: Remove (None / Person /
Foreground, the last enabled for pictures only), Feather, and the analysis's
progress and its finding.

**Proof** (`e9_proof.py` over MCP, `e9_probe.py`): the "no subject" rule on
a UI recording — cut and uncut byte-identical; a still of a person
(`/System/Library/Photos/Resources/FlexAudio/` and Adobe CEP's hero image
exist on this host and carry no personal data — the spike's fixtures) cut
with `foreground` makes the masked pixels transparent and the rest the
backdrop; registration through a crop, a spotlight zoom and a portrait
(rotated) source; a pending instant draws uncut; the cache survives a moved
package and a relink rebuilds it; `foreground` on a media clip refused by
name; two runs of the analysis write byte-identical PNGs on the proof
machine. Mutants: the window rule made per-frame; `orientedUV` skipped; the
device left unpinned; `.fast` substituted.

**Limits.** Person segmentation misses backlit, from-behind and small
figures (0–3.9 % where foreground found the whole figure, §5b). Mask quality
on real camera footage — hair, motion blur — is unmeasured and is a check
for a person at the machine. No brush refinement and no tracking of a
chosen subject (D5). An hour of source is about twelve minutes of analysis.

# Spec §11 — decisions: Mattes (#240, road map "mattes")

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed: its condensed record is `designs/adr/mattes.md`, and the
original, `archive/mattes.md`, holds each phase's record (MT0–MT5). MT-1..MT-6 were recorded in
MT0, before any code, and MT-6's choice of route was filled from MT0's spike
(`tools/proof/matte_spike/`); MT-7 (the chrome) was recorded at MT4's start, before its code.
They are not G- decisions: a matte is a track relation the compositor draws for any clip, not a
graphics decision (road map 10's own plan: "Mattes are compositor features",
`designs/adr/svg-motion-plan.md`). The video-input half of #240 is #251, and nothing here decides
it.

- **MT-1 — A matte is a track relation in a closed vocabulary, drawn by the one compositor; R5-1
  and G-1 stand.** A track's `matte` is `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or
  `luma_inverted`, set by `set_track {matte}` (`none` switches it off). A matte track's clips are
  never drawn on the canvas; at each instant what they show cuts every layer the track directly
  behind draws (MT-2). Any clip that draws can be one — text, shape, image, graphic, video, nest.
  Nothing is a package, a shader or an expression, and a graphic on a matte track is called with
  the same arguments and keyed the same way as anywhere (G-5, G-9 untouched). A clip is a matte
  only by the track it is on: moved off, it is ordinary; the tracks `paste` adds are ordinary;
  `duplicate` keeps its track. Persisted as `tracks[].matte`, written only when not `none` — the
  model's first `skip_serializing_if`, so every older file and every ordinary track round-trips
  byte for byte and the reader's default is the same answer. `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` 14, no migrate
  step. The video half of #240 is #251 and nothing here decides it.
- **MT-2 — What a matte cuts, and when it cuts nothing.** Its target is the track directly behind
  it in its own container (the timeline, or one nest's own tracks) when that track is not itself
  a matte track. With no such track (the back-most track, or a matte behind it) a matte cuts
  nothing and its clips still draw nothing. Where the matte track shows nothing at an instant — no
  clip, the track hidden, a clip's video off — the track behind shows uncut (owner, 2026-10-07,
  choice 5). Read per instant and per pair of tracks: no clip names another, so split, move,
  delete, paste, nest and undo cannot break a link; `add_track`, `move_track` and `remove_track`
  change which track is behind, visibly. A matte track's clips sound as on any track, and Mute
  Audio silences them (owner, 2026-10-08, O1): a matte is a picture rule, like Hide Video.
- **MT-3 — The four modes, and where the cut is applied.** At a pixel the matte's composite —
  premultiplied, in encoded sRGB like every stage of the compositor (§7.5) — gives: `alpha` its
  alpha a; `alpha_inverted` 1 − a; `luma` the Rec. 709 luma (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, the weights
  the shader's saturation uses) of its premultiplied colour, so transparent counts as black;
  `luma_inverted` 1 − that. The value multiplies the matted layer's coverage at the fragment
  stage's step 7, beside the corner radius and the nest clip rectangle, sampled at the fragment's
  own canvas position. So the matted clip's own drop shadow follows the cut-out shape (its
  silhouette pass runs the same stage; owner choice 6), and its reflection is cut by the matte
  where the reflection lands — under an alpha matte, a reflection outside the window is gone — as
  the nest clip rectangle already cuts one (owner, 2026-10-08, O10). The outgoing half of a
  dissolve multiplies its partner's cover by the same value — on one matted track both halves are
  cut by the same matte — which keeps a dissolve under a soft matte exact. `TrackMatte`'s
  declaration order is a shader discriminant (`none` 0 to `luma_inverted` 4): append only.
- **MT-4 — A matte clip's own properties (owner, 2026-10-07, choice 6).** Its placement, crop,
  corner radius, opacity, colour, chroma, filters, spotlight, obscured regions, motion presets,
  actions and transitions with other matte clips shape the matte, because it is drawn by the
  ordinary layer pass. Its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing: the CORE emits a
  matte layer with `blend: "normal"`, `shadow: null` and `reflection: null`, the recipe's second
  deliberate override of model values after a transition's `normal` (§7.3). The inspector shows
  the model's values and says they are not drawn (MT-7). Amends G-10's "blend … apply" for a
  graphic on a matte track.
- **MT-5 — Mattes in nests.** The rule holds in every container. Walking from a layer's own track
  outward through the nest clips it is inside, the first level whose track is a matte track makes
  the layer draw into that matte (or nowhere, when the matte has no target or cuts no layer at
  that instant), and no level outside that applies to the layer; every level inside it whose
  track is a matte's target cuts the layer, each matte multiplying in. One matte is keyed by (the
  ids of the nest clips enclosing its track's container, outermost first — the instance path's
  prefix — and the matte track's id), so two clips showing the same nest at one instant (a split
  nest clip in a dissolve) each have their own matte. A nest clip on a matte track makes its whole
  composite the matte (a matte inside it included), and a nest clip on a matted track has every
  layer it draws cut — at a soft edge, overlapping inner layers show through each other, the
  recorded limit of nest opacity (§7.3). `nest` puts the nest clip on the front-most selected
  track that is not a matte track (the front-most when all are), and gives a nested track its
  source track's matte only when the nested track directly behind it is the copy of that matte's
  target. A selection that takes a matte's clips without its target, beside other clips, is
  nested as asked: the matte clips draw inside the nest and the picture changes; undo restores
  (owner, 2026-10-08, O9). `unnest` lines up the nest's front-most NON-matte track (the
  front-most when all are) with the nest clip's track, so carried matte tracks land on the tracks
  in front of it and nest-then-unnest restores the picture; it makes no track a matte, so a matte
  clip with no track in front lands on a new ordinary track, as any clip refused on the way out
  does.
- **MT-6 — How the compositor draws a matte.** Before the destination pass opens, each matte the
  recipe lists (`mattes`, deepest container first) is drawn by the ordinary layer pipelines into
  a destination-sized `bgra8Unorm` target, so a matte never suspends the destination pass as a
  shadow does. Each distinct set of mattes a layer is cut by is resolved into one
  destination-sized `r8Unorm` coverage texture, cleared to 1, each matte's mode multiplied in by a
  full-frame pass. The layer stage samples it at `texture(1)` at the fragment's
  canvas-normalised position, so Preview Quality, a shadow's canvas-sized silhouette pass, a
  reflection and every export read one coverage. An unmatted layer binds the existing 1×1 white
  placeholder at `texture(1)`, chosen by MT0's spike (2026-10-08; Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1,
  `pmset` powermode 0, on AC power; 200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of the
  runs' medians): one full-bleed unmatted layer (S1) cost 0.014 ms more than the tree's shader
  with the placeholder route and 0.019 ms more with the function-constant route at 1920×1080,
  against a V0-against-V0 noise floor of 0.038 ms, and 0.052 ms and −0.003 ms more at 3840×2160,
  against 0.002 ms — the placeholder within its bound plus the noise at both sizes (0.02 ms at
  1080p, 0.08 ms at 4K). With it a matte cost (S3 − S2, the text as an alpha matte) −0.082 ms at
  1080p, a negative figure larger than that size's noise floor, so the 1080p series do not
  resolve a matte's cost, and 0.066 ms at 4K; two mattes in one coverage (S4 − S2)
  0.040 ms and 0.542 ms, within the 0.50 ms and 2.00 ms budget. Risk accepted: at 4K every
  unmatted full-bleed layer pays 0.05–0.07 ms for the sample (S1: 0.052 ms over the tree's
  shader; two layers, S2: 0.887 ms with the placeholder against 0.752 ms with the function
  constant), for one pipeline per layer
  specialization instead of two. `LayerUniforms` stays 104 floats. Targets are pooled per destination
  size and allocated on the first matted frame (at 3840×2160, 33.2 MB per matte and 8.3 MB per
  coverage). (Amended by PR-1: each matte's composite is `rgba16Float`, 66.4 MB at 3840×2160;
  the `r8Unorm` coverage and its 8.3 MB stand.) The deferred E5 and E9 take the next free texture slots.
- **MT-7 — The chrome (owner, 2026-10-08, O2–O8).** No fifth header toggle and no shortcut. Set
  by Track ▸ Matte ▸ Off / Alpha / Inverted Alpha / Luma / Inverted Luma on the current track,
  and by the same submenu in the track's context menu after Solo, each checked for the track's
  mode; undo "Track Matte"; re-choosing the current mode is an identity. The header shows a
  tag by the name — "Matte · Alpha", "Matte · Inverted Alpha", "Matte · Luma", "Matte ·
  Inverted Luma" — in the primary label colour over a faint accent tint, so its legibility never
  depends on the accent the person picked; dimmed (muted words, a fainter tint) and reading
  "Matte · nothing behind" when the track has no target (MT-2); on its own line under the name when the row leaves room above the toggles (every Medium
  and Large row, and the Small video row), else on the name's line, right-aligned, the name
  clipped before it — and there, when its full words would leave the name less than 40 pt, the
  tag reads "Matte" alone. A matte track's clips are drawn at half opacity with a dashed outline,
  and an accent bracket joins its lane to
  the track below when it has a target. Every Clip sub-tab opens with a note when every selected
  clip sits on a matte track and those tracks share one mode: "Matte for the track below
  (<mode>). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect.", or, when none
  of those tracks has a target, "Nothing is behind this matte track, so it cuts nothing."; every
  control stays live, its values kept for when the track stops being a matte. On the canvas a
  matte clip is the topmost hit inside its box, selected and dragged like any clip.
- **MT-8 — A dissolve or zoom with a nested half mixes its two halves exactly, matte or not
  (#252; owner, 2026-10-08; zoom by the owner's residue rule, 2026-10-08).** A `cross_dissolve`
  or `zoom` whose container is a nest, or one of whose two clips is a nest clip, is ROUTED. Each
  half is drawn, with no dissolve weight, into its own destination-sized `bgra8Unorm` target
  cleared transparent. (Amended by PR-1: the halves are `rgba16Float`, so the memory figures
  below double.) A half is everything its clip draws: inner layers, their mattes, shadows
  and reflections, and any dissolve inside it, each such level in a pair of targets of its own.
  One full-frame pass then lays the pair on what is below as (1 − p)·out + p·in, source-over. So
  the frame is (1 − p)·H_out + p·H_in + (1 − (1 − p)·a_out − p·a_in)·D, with H each half's
  premultiplied picture drawn alone, a its alpha and D what is behind. A zoom's halves are
  scaled in that pass, out by 1 + 0.25p and in by 0.75 + 0.25p (the vertex stage's own ramps),
  each about its half's anchor — the canvas point its clip is placed at: a plain clip's anchor,
  or the centre of a nest clip's placed canvas rectangle — and sampled bilinearly from its
  target, transparent outside it; H is then the scaled half. So a nested zoom's half zooms as
  one picture about the nest clip's centre, where each inner layer used to scale about its own
  anchor, and it is resampled once from its target, where an unnested zoom scales each layer
  from its source. That holds for nest → plain, plain → nest, nest ↔ nest and a dissolve inside
  a nest, under any mattes, in the canvas pass and in a matte's own. The core decides it (§7.3).
  A routed level is an entry in the layer's `dissolve`, never its `transition`, and its layers
  draw `normal` as a transition's do. A layer drawn into a matte keeps only the dissolves at or
  inside its first matte level, so a matte inside a dissolving nest clip is drawn whole and the
  half fades once. The overlapping inner layers of a half no longer show through each other
  mid-dissolve. Every nested dissolve's and zoom's picture changed, which the owner accepted. A
  timeline dissolve or zoom between two clips that are not nest clips keeps MT-3's per-layer
  correction and is unchanged. Push, slide, wipe and the fades are not routed: they apply no
  partner correction to dip. Cost, from MT-9's pool, shared with the mattes:
  - Memory: two targets per routed dissolve, live from its first half's draw to its mix (66.4 MB
    at 3840×2160, 16.6 MB at 1920×1080), and two more for each routed dissolve inside a half.
  - Passes, per routed dissolve: the pass it lands in is suspended and resumed once, two passes
    are cleared and stored, and one full-frame draw is added. The halves' own layers draw once,
    as before.

  A frame with no routed dissolve pays nothing. `LayerUniforms` and the layer stage's texture
  slots are unchanged. A half that is one layer could be drawn straight onto the pass with its
  correction read from the other half's target, saving one target. That route was not taken: it
  would cost every layer draw a third texture sample, MT-6's measured placeholder cost. Measured
  before and after by `matte_proof.py` D0–D8 (issue batch B90).
- **MT-9 — The matte pool keeps what recent frames used, and no cap drops a picture (#253;
  owner, 2026-10-08).** Amends MT-6's pooling sentence.
  - **Planning.** A frame's mattes are planned before any is drawn (`MattePlan`). Each cut set
    is resolved as soon as the last matte it names is drawn. A matte's `bgra8Unorm` composite
    goes back to the pool once every cut set naming it is resolved, so a later matte in the same
    frame draws into it. A frame therefore holds as many composites at once as mattes are live
    (one, for any number of mattes that each cut their own set). It also holds one `r8Unorm`
    coverage per distinct cut set, and those all outlive the destination pass.
  - **Between frames.** A frame is one `render` call. The pool keeps, of each kind, as many
    targets as the most any of the renderer's last 30 frames held at once
    (`MattePool.keepFrames`), and releases the rest when a frame ends. A frame with no matte
    counts as holding none, and a destination size change still empties the pool. At 3840×2160,
    ten matte pairs in one frame hold 33.2 MB + 10 × 8.3 MB = 116.1 MB, where MT-6's pool held
    414.7 MB. (Amended by PR-1: the composite is `rgba16Float`, 66.4 MB at 3840×2160, so ten
    matte pairs hold 66.4 MB + 10 × 8.3 MB = 149.4 MB, where MT-6's pool would hold 746.5 MB; the
    coverage's 8.3 MB stands.)
  - **No cap.** A frame that needs more targets gets them, and a target Metal cannot make fails
    the frame as before (`MatteError.noTarget`). A renderer that stops drawing keeps what its
    last 30 frames held until it draws again or is released with its player item or export.

# 1. What this is

A screencast editor without a recorder — and, since road map 3,
a recorder of the SCREEN, and since §11 CAM-1 of a camera beside it or on its
own, whose output is ordinary media. Open one or
more video files from disk, arrange them on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim,
split, annotate, animate, and export. Mac only, Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

Deliberate non-goals: multicam, color grading beyond
per-clip controls (§11 GR-1: tier 1 of grading — tone, adjustment clips,
looks, LUT import, an ungraded switch and one luma waveform — is in, kept by
the owner's verdict of 2026-10-10, and tier 2's scopes, colour wheels,
curves and qualifiers beside it, GR-10…GR-13; tier 3's HDR→SDR conversion
and camera log are in, GR-15, GR-16; the HDR road map's HLG timeline, its
HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, HDR scopes, the PQ peak, Canon Log
2 and 3 and opt-in linear-light blending are in, HD-1…HD-17; a wide-gamut
working space for SDR projects is not wanted, GR-20; tier 4's vectorscope zoom,
hue curves, the blend between curves of different point counts and the
qualifier's cleanup blur are in, GR-24, GR-31…GR-35, while an Offset
wheel, a qualifier on picture clips, 1,024-level scopes and a histogram
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), a plugin system (a clip may
draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package, road map 10; nothing
else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.
**Audio beyond what shipped was on it too until §11 AU-2** (road map
"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

**The opening flow is the point.** File > Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a
drop on the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an
*untitled* project sized to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source. The app is also the Alternate handler for movie, audio and image
types so Open With… works from the Finder.

content.content:
- **CAM-1 — Camera recording is IN; callouts stay OUT** (the owner, 2026-10-26, reversing the camera half of recording.md's first bullet and §1's non-goal). Frame Job records a camera on its own, or at the same time as a screen recording (a talking head over a screencast). The owner's four answers, as given: 1. **Camera alone, or camera at the same time as a screen recording.** Each capture lands as its own file on its own track. With a screen recording the camera goes on a track ABOVE the screen, placed as a corner picture-in-picture that can be moved; the corner, the scale and the inset are CR3's to decide. 2. **The entry is the existing recorder panel**: a Camera source, and a camera row when recording the screen. One panel, one countdown, one menu-bar status item with Pause and Stop, the same landing into the project. File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) stays the one door. 3. **Devices**: built-in and USB/UVC cameras and iPhone Continuity Camera; a live preview of the chosen camera in the panel; a choice of resolution and frame rate from the camera's formats, otherwise its best format. 4. **Audio**: the chosen microphone (which can be the camera's own) is its own audio file on its own track, lined up to the picture, as screen recording does today. Everything else recording.md decided carries over: a recording is ordinary media, the files live in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, the panel asks for the grants and the tool never does, the microphone is a second file, a pause is a sequence of files, one grouped edit lands everything, and every door has an MCP mirror (a new source is an argument of `record_screen`, the voice-over's precedent, unless a phase records otherwise). Callouts stay out for the reason recording.md gives: a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant. **Risk accepted:** a second capture stack (`AVCaptureSession` for a camera) beside ScreenCaptureKit, a Camera grant and its entitlement, and a camera's own clock to line up with the screen's and the microphone's; CR0 measures each before any of it is built. - **CAM-2 — The camera spike's rule (CR0), fixed before its run.** `tools/proof/camera_spike/` - **CAM-10 — A camera beside the screen lands, and `record_screen` records it (CR3b), recorded before its code; amends CAM-4 (2), CAM-6 (6) and CAM-9 (10).** A screen recording's `(Camera).mov` files (CAM-9) land in the same grouped edit as its movies and microphone files, and the tool admits `camera` and `camera_format` with source `screen`. CAM-3 to CAM-9 stand except where this entry amends them. 1. **The track.** ONE new track at the open container's FRONT (its index is the container's track count after the pictures have landed), named "Camera", added on the attempt of the first camera clip that takes a frame and kept only when that clip lands (`addMicrophones`' attempt pattern), so a recording none of whose camera files makes a clip adds no track. 2. **Time.** Segment k's camera clip is asked at `screenStart_k + cameraOffset_k`, its floor `max(screenStart_k, the previous camera clip's end)`. A start below the floor is head-trimmed to it by the microphone's shared dance (`headTrimmed`: add at the floor, `trim_start`, move back, read back, a second try a frame up at an inexact rate). CR3a measured every `cameraOffset` negative, so the trim is the usual path. A camera wholly under its head lands as media only with " was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of it would remain after the ms head that keeps it clear of ." A screen picture that minted no clip still gives its `at`. A segment LEFT OUT because its screen movie would not probe (`UnreadableSegment`) keeps its camera file on disk, named in `kept_files` and its left-out sentence (CAM-9 (7)), and never lands it; only its microphone takes the slot (#181 item 2), so the camera's starts are read off the `.segment(k)` stretches alone. 3. **The corner.** With the container's canvas `cw × ch` (inside an open nest, the nest's) and the camera file's `sw × sh`: `s = clamp(min(0.25·cw/sw, ch/(3·sh)), 0.01, 10)` — the box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, the core's scale range — `x = (cw/2 − 0.05·cw − sw·s/2).rounded()` and `y = (ch/2 − 0.05·ch − sh·s/2).rounded()`, in the C frame (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`: an offset of the layer's centre from the canvas centre, y down). So the picture sits in the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner, inside the 90 % ring of View ▸ Safe Areas (the guide spec §4.1 names title-safe; the industry's action-safe). One `set_video {x, y, scale}` per clip, right after its placement; nothing else is set, and the clip stays an ordinary clip a person moves. 4. **One grouped edit**, in the order pictures → cameras → microphones. `place: false` lands the camera media with no clip and no track. A new project lands the cameras through `remainderPlacement`, after the later pictures; without clip 1, as media only with its `unplacedNote`. For ONE segment that undo step is "Add Camera and Microphone" with a camera and any voice (its own or a left-out segment's), "Add Camera" with a camera alone, and otherwise as before ("Add Microphone", "Add Recording Segments"). 5. **The tool.** `camera` and `camera_format` are admitted with source `screen`, lifting CAM-4 (2) and CAM-6 (6) for it. With source screen, a `camera_format` given without `camera` is refused in CAM-4 (2)'s step (3): "With source screen, camera_format needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen." With source voice_over the given ones of `camera`, `camera_format` are refused there together: "With source voice_over, cannot be given — a voice-over records the microphone alone." (CAM-4 (2)'s "only source camera records a camera" is no longer true.) The order after step (5): (6) `project`; (7) the camera lookup and its format — for a screen recording too, when `camera` is given; (8) the Camera grant; then, for a screen, the Screen Recording grant and the display or window lookup; (9) the recording. The tool never prepares a capture or adopts one (CAM-7 (7)). 6. **The answer.** Per `segments[k]` and never at the top level: `camera_path`, `camera_duration` and `camera_offset` when that segment has a camera file; `camera_problem` and `camera_note` when set; `camera_media` and `camera_clip` when known. The top-level `camera` is CAM-4 (6)'s, unchanged. `note` gains every segment's `cameraProblem` then `cameraNote`, in order, after `camera.problem` and `camera.note`. 7. **The stop wait** counts three probes per segment with a camera beside the screen (`finishCeiling + 3 × probeTimeout × max(n, 1) + 5`), and its timeout sentence names the camera files after the movies (" Its camera file is at ." / " Its camera files are at , ."), read from the recorder's held camera paths. 8. **The readers.** With a camera BESIDE the screen the panel's landing note says the display's `.systemStopped` sentence (not the camera's) and puts `camera.problem` after the microphone's problem; every segment's `cameraProblem` and `cameraNote` lead the placement's notes, and follow `camera.note` in a failed landing's note. `filesClause` adds " and its camera at

" or " and its camera files at , " after the microphone clause. 9. **No panel door yet.** The recorder panel offers no camera with a screen source until CR3c (CAM-11); until then the tool is the one door that records a camera beside the screen. - **CAM-11 — The panel's camera beside the screen (CR3c), recorded before its code; amends CAM-5 (2), CAM-6 (2), CAM-7 (1) and (3), and CAM-10 (7) and (9).** With a display or the Window row chosen, the recorder panel offers a "Record the camera too" checkbox; ticked, the panel records the chosen camera at the chosen format beside the screen (CAM-9, CAM-10). CAM-3 to CAM-10 stand except where this entry amends them. 1. **The box** is a grid row with no label, directly under Include Frame Job windows and above Camera. It is enabled only while idle with a display row or the Window row; under Camera or Microphone Only it is greyed with its value kept. It is a control of its own: an "Off" row in the Camera popup would change what the shared camera key means for Source Camera and for hot-plug (CAM-8). 2. **The key.** `FrameJobRecordingCameraBeside`, a Bool, off when absent, is written by `persistChoices` on every change and read by `restoreChoices`. It persists across launches, unlike the session-only Camera row; it is the panel's tenth `FrameJobRecording…` key, pinned in the harness and `screens.py`. A hot-plug writes nothing (CAM-8 (4)). 3. **A camera wanted** means Source Camera, or the box ticked with a display row or the Window row. Then the Camera and Format popups are live while idle (amending CAM-5 (2) and CAM-6 (2)'s "only while idle with Source Camera"). `currentChoice()` carries `camera` (the popup's id) and `cameraFormat` (nil for Best) beside a `.display` or `.picked` source; otherwise `camera` is nil, as before. With the box ticked, System Audio, Show Clicks, Size, Include Frame Job windows and Rate stay live, and the size note is the screen's. 4. **The preview** (amending CAM-7 (1) and (3)). The well's row is shown, and CAM-7's step runs, whenever a camera is wanted; step (1) reads "the panel not visible or closing, or no camera wanted → off". Step (2) also covers a screen recording's camera beside it: that capture's layer, else "The camera is recording.". `prepareCamera` acts for any choice naming a camera whose source is not `.voiceOver`. The countdown keeps that capture, and the panel's `start(…, mayAsk: true)` adopts it (CAM-9 (1)); a tool start never does (CAM-7 (7)). 5. **The press with the box ticked**, in order: (1) Window… with nothing picked gives its sentence; (2) no camera gives "No camera is connected."; (3) the Screen Recording grant; (4) the Camera grant, asked from `notDetermined`, `Privacy_Camera` opened when denied or restricted, and a prompt's answer re-read before the microphone is checked (CAM-5 (4)); (5) the Microphone grant; (6) the countdown. With the box off nothing changes, and the Camera grant is never read. 6. **The recording** is a screen recording: the panel orders out (`hidesForRecording` unchanged), the status item is its chrome, and it lands by CAM-10. 7. **The timeout sentence** (amending CAM-10 (7)) spells the ceiling the stop wait used — its `camera:` is the wait's own `cameraBeside` — even when the recorder holds no camera file. 8. **CAM-10 (9) is lifted.** The box is the panel's door to a camera beside the screen, and the catalog's `record_screen` description and the guide name it.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
  and `media_converted_by`.
- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`
  for an audio row and for every row of an SDR project, else the picture:
  the six HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) carry
  `hlg` (the default), `pq` or `sdr`, every other video row writes the SDR
  version, and `hlg`/`pq` are refused in an SDR project and on any other row, each in its own sentence.
- `av1_mp4.rs` · `ffi_av1.rs` — AV1 in MP4 (spec §11 CX-12, road map
  codec-export C1): `av1C` built from a full parse of the sequence header OBU,
  temporal delimiters stripped in place, and the `av01` brand put into `ftyp`
  (no `mp41` to replace is an error, never a file without `av01`); the three
  `rc_av1_*` exports. `leb128` is shared with `hdr10.rs`. The export table's
  `writer` field (`svt_av1` on `av1` and `av1_webm`; `avf_preset` stays the ImageIO
  switch) and the `encoder_speed` override (`faster` | `balanced` | `smaller`,
  refused on any other row) are `export_table.rs`' and `export_overrides.rs`';
  `Container` is `export_container.rs`'.
- `export_encoder.rs` — the bundled encoders' route and speeds (spec §11
  CX-12, CX-16): `Writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; none is AVFoundation; `takes_speed`
  false for libvpx's one speed) and `EncoderSpeed`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C3's toll, a pure move) and re-exported there.

(HD-20) is the third export, over `hdr10_still.rs`.
- `hdr10_still.rs` — a PQ still's HDR10 peak (spec §11 HD-20, #325): a PNG's
  `cLLI`/`mDCV` chunks before the first IDAT, else a HEIF/AVIF primary item's
  `clli`/`mdcv` properties (its first `ipma`); MaxCLL first, the same rounding
  and clamp as `hdr10.rs`. Pure, every index checked against the buffer.
- `model_matte.rs` — the matte vocabulary (format version 14, spec §11 MT-1):
  `TrackMatte` (`none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma`, `luma_inverted`)
  and `is_none`, re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD
  `Track.matte` stays in `model_track.rs`, skipped when `none` (an ordinary
  track writes no key), as `ColorAdjust`'s nine tone keys are when 0.
- `model_color.rs` — `normalise_color`, G-12's colour grammar (hex,
  `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `hsl()`/`hsla()` and the CSS named colours, from
  svgtypes' table) to lowercase `#rrggbb[aa]`; out of range is refused,
  never clamped. The stdlib's `__parseColour` implements the same grammar,
  and both suites read `graphic/tests/colours.json`. `rc_normalise_color`
  (`ffi.rs`) exports it for the Inspector's colour defaults (spec §11 G-25
  (c)), and `model_graphic.rs`'s `check_schema` refuses a `color` default
  it refuses (G-25 (a)). `color_channels` and `color_hex` (which
  `normalise_color` writes through) and `oklab_mix` are
  `actions_graphic.rs`'s blend's: `oklab_mix` is the stdlib's
  `interpolateColors` ported operation for operation (spec §11 G-40), now
  bytes/255 through `oklab_mix_unit` and ×255 rounded out; `oklab_mix_unit`
  and `oklab_mix_rgb` (0–1 floats, clamped, never rounded) are
  `actions_color.rs`'s (G-43). Three suites read `graphic/tests/oklab.json`:

  `recipe_text.rs` — `frame_recipe(t)`: the layer list at one instant. `RecipeLayer`

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never

  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and

  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,

  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a

  `.graphicsLocationDidChange`), the scan (each legal `*.js` with its

  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**The core's edge.**

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).
