# 5.4 Actions

`Action { start (clip time), duration, curve, end: Patch }`. To evaluate a
property at clip time *t*: start from the clip's base props, apply the end
patch of every action that finished at or before *t* (in start order),
then if *t* is inside an action, interpolate from that state to the
action's end patch along its curve. Numeric fields interpolate; colors
interpolate in OKLab with straight alpha, known by key — `video.shadow.color`,
`video.chroma.key` (rgb only), `text.color`, `text.outline.color`,
`text.backdrop.color`, `text.word_style.active_color`, `.spoken_color`,
`.upcoming_color` and `text.word_style.active_pill.color`; a key whose ends
are equal stays exact (§11 G-43); booleans and strings switch at the end. Actions
on a clip may not overlap (`add_action` refuses). Video, audio and text
properties all go through the one list with typed patches.

**The timeline's volume line is a view of actions, not keyframes** (§11
AU-80…AU-83). It draws the plan's gain for a clip; a drag on it writes the
clip's `set_audio {volume}` or the end of the action whose `audio.volume`
is in force, and a point added with ⌥ is an action's END: `add_action` from
the latest action end before the press, or — inside an action whose end
names only `audio.volume` — `set_action` shortening it and `add_action` for
the rest, which carries its end volume and its curve (so an eased action's
shape is re-eased on each side). Nothing is stored that actions do not
already store; an agent makes the same point with those ops.

**Every audio setting the tap runs animates too** (§11 AU-85…AU-88): the
pan, the mono fold, the channel pick, the EQ, the hum notch, noise
reduction, the gate, the leveller's target and limits (§11 AU-66), the de-esser, the
compressor, the limiter and isolation's Amount. The plan carries each audio segment's points — the
clip's evaluated audio at the voice's ends, each such action's ends and the
1/30 s grid inside an eased one (§7.2) — and the tap joins them with straight
lines on an absolute sample grid, so the preview and an export agree. The
rule is the one above, with two additions: `isolation` is present at 0, so an
action toward 0.8 ramps from 0; and an EQ slope, the hum's mains and its
harmonics are switches, held until the action's end. Volume, the fades and
ducking were already the envelope's; the duck, `keep_pitch`, the fade
shapes, the voice effect and a nest clip's own keys are not animated. A gate
or limiter keyed on at an end runs for the whole track from then, and an
isolation render is made for a clip whose base Amount is 0 when an end asks
for one.

**A graphic clip's props are a fourth target** (format version 13, §11
G-34), with a door of its own: an end's `graphic: {props, kinds}`. A
`number` ramps and arrives fractional, never rounded; a `color` ramps in
OKLab with straight alpha, as `interpolateColors` blends (§11 G-40;
`#00000000` to `#ffffff` is `#63636380` halfway); a `string`, `boolean`,
`enum` or `asset` switches at the end, and `""` is no image in an end
(§11 G-42); a prop whose schema entry says `animate: false` is refused
(§11 G-41).
A colour is known by the end's `kinds`, never by the value's shape; two
numbers ramp whatever `kinds` holds. The props a patch names are checked
against the op's `schema`; a stored end is never re-checked.

**A media clip's rate is a fifth target** (format version 27, §11 SR-10):
`speed`, a number at the top of an end beside the groups. The rule above on
one number: the rate in force is the clip's `speed`, then each ended
action's `end.speed` in start order; inside the first action spanning *t*,
when it names a speed, `r_from + (r_to − r_from)·ease(u)`; held after. An
action ending at the rate already in force changes nothing. The clip keeps
its slot: the rate changes how much source it reads, `S(t) = ∫₀ᵗ rate`, in
closed form per curve (∫₀ᵘ ease: u²/2, u³/3, u² − u³/3, u³ − u⁴/2), so its
out point is `in + round(S(duration))`, and an action edit that would read
past the media's end is refused (§6). Only a `media` clip ramps; a `speed`
in any other clip's end, or one that is not a number, is inert.

**Lists interpolate per index** when the two sides are the same length and
each pair of entries agrees on the keys that say WHAT the entry is — a
filter's `kind`, a region's `kind` and `shape` — and switch at the end
otherwise; the hold is per entry, so a list in which one region changes
shape still interpolates every region beside it. That is the crate's rule
and not one list's (`actions.rs`), so `video.filters` and `video.obscure`
are both governed by it with no code of their own. The wider set of
discriminants is deliberately confined to list ENTRIES: in a list an
entry's only identity is its index, so a changed `shape` gives no way to
tell a reshaped region from a replaced one, while `video.spotlight` is one
named object whose `shape` is a property of it — an action that moves that
spotlight from a rect to an ellipse still interpolates its geometry, as it
always did.

**A curve's points interpolate per point** (format 17, §11 GR-12): a channel
of `video.curves` is a list of `[x, y]` pairs, so the list rule above lerps
two curves of the same count point by point, and a convex mix of two rising
x sequences still rises. One rule is the curves' own (`actions_curves.rs`):
before the lerp, a channel that is the **identity** on one side (absent
included — the state writes an absent channel as `[[0, 0], [1, 1]]`) and a
curve of a different count on the other is **aligned**: the identity side
takes the other curve's x's with y = x, its first point `[0, 0]` and its last
`[1, 1]`, so a grade animates from neutral, and back to it. Two non-identity
curves of different counts **blend their values** (§11 GR-34): the list rule
holds the list at its start value `a`, so the evaluated props hold `a`, and
the recipe and `clip_state` publish the channel as `{from: a, to: b, t}` for
0 < t < 1 (t the eased progress), which the compositor draws as
`(1 − t)·a(x) + t·b(x)`, exact at both ends. The core samples no spline and
the blend is never in a file: a split mid-blend writes `a` as the head's end,
and the tail blends `a → b` over the rest. An identity curve in an END patch
is kept as written and means "animate to neutral" (a `null` there would remove the key,
the rule below); the inspector's Reset inside an action writes it so. The
evaluated end is clamped like every other value, and an identity channel
evaluates to none.

The hue curves (format 20, §11 GR-32), `hue_hue` and `hue_sat`, follow the
same rules in their own units: two of the same count lerp per point (x
linearly, never across 0°/360°); an identity (every value the neutral, the
state writing an absent one as `[[0, 0], [180, 0]]` or `[[0, 1], [180, 1]]`)
meeting a curve of another count takes that curve's x's with the neutral
value; two non-identity hue curves of different counts blend their values
(§11 GR-34), in degrees or as a gain.

**A qualifier's hue centre takes the short way round** (format 18, §11 GR-13):
two present ranges of `video.qualifier` interpolate per number, but a hue
centre is an angle, and 350 → 10 lerped as numbers would sweep through 180.
Before the lerp (`actions_qualifier.rs`), when both states hold a centre more
than 180° apart, the TARGET's centre moves by ±360 (350 → 370), and the
evaluated end's clamp brings the lerped value back into [0, 360) (`rem_euclid
360`): 350 → 10 passes 355, 0, 5. Two centres exactly 180° apart go linearly.
Only the target of the action the time is inside is touched; an ended
action's end is merged as written. A range turned on or off, and `invert`,
switch at the end — a key on one side only holds until then (the object rule
below walks the FROM side's keys). The cleanup blur (format 21, §11 GR-35)
animates whenever both states hold a qualifier: `video_json` writes a
non-neutral qualifier with its `blur` present even at 0
(`actions_qualifier.rs`'s `qualifier_json`), so 0 → 0.5 reads 0.25 halfway; a
qualifier turned on switches at the end.

The object rule is why `text.animation`'s discriminant is spelled `kind`
(format version 5): an action from a typewriter to a line rise switches at
the end, where an action between two typewriters of different lengths
interpolates their `in` and `out`. That second one is legal and rarely what
anybody wants — the two numbers are the animation's own timebase, so
sliding them mid-reveal moves the ground under it — which is a caution, not
a rule the ops enforce.

**`video.motion` is NOT an animation target** (format version 8). A preset is
anchored to the clip's two ends and an action is a ramp between two states,
so there is nothing to interpolate — half a slide into half a spin is not a
picture anybody asked for — and the evaluator would put the base value back
anyway, leaving a control that reported success and did nothing. So
`set_action_end` refuses a patch whose `video` object names `motion`, by
name — the one refusal that is about the OP rather than about the
vocabulary, since the patch is otherwise walked like any other; and
because a hand-written file, a pasted action or a project from another tool
reaches evaluation without passing the op, `evaluate_clip` overwrites the
state's `motion` with the BASE value's JSON before the video group is
decoded. That restore is at the `Value` level for two reasons — `clamp_video`
is never handed the base props, and a malformed `motion` would otherwise fail
the whole group's decode and discard every other animated property — and it
is GUARDED on the group still being an object, since an end patch may have
replaced `video` with a number, a string, an array, a bool or a null and each
of those must keep falling through to the base props exactly as it always
did.

An action's end patch is **walked like every other patch** and lenient about
VALUES. `set_action_end` refuses an unknown key, a value of the wrong JSON
kind and a misspelt variant, naming the dotted path with the group's name in
it (`unknown key "video.filters[1].kindd" in an action end patch`) and the
value sent — the three groups it may name are `video`, `audio` and `text`,
and a graphic clip's props are a fourth target with a door of its own
(above), and a `null` at any depth REMOVES that key rather than clearing
the property, so it is the one value the walk always lets past. What it
does not do is range-check (except a graphic prop's end, §11 G-34 (c)):
the state a clip interpolates toward may legitimately name a value no
stored group could hold, and a half-written animation must stay
editable, where `set_video` and its siblings are **strict** and name an
out-of-range value. Forward compatibility — a project a NEWER build wrote —
is the FILE reader's, which keeps an `end` object exactly as it found it.
The evaluator is therefore the last line of defence: `frame_recipe` and
`clip_state` clamp every value they produce to the same table the ops
enforce (opacity 0–1, scale 0.01–10, gain 0–4, non-negative radii and
crops) and collapse a NaN to that field's neutral value. The compositor
never has to defend itself, and one bad number cannot blank a frame.

**A STORED `null` on an optional key is "off at the end"** (§11 CI-14): an
end state holding `"shadow": null` switches the shadow off when the action
finishes — the evaluator already switches a `null` at the end, and the
removal rule above leaves a stored `null` alone. A `null` in a PATCH cannot
write one, because there it is a removal, so `set_action_end` takes a second
argument, `off`: a list of `"group.key"` paths, each written as a `null`
into the end state after the patch is merged — and `audio.eq.<slot>`, one
of the EQ's seven slots keyed off inside the end's `eq` (§11 AU-88), the one
deeper path. `off` refuses what `patch`
refuses — `video.motion`, `text.words`, a key the group does not have, and a
REQUIRED key (`video.opacity`, `video.crop`), whose `null` no group can
hold — plus a malformed path and a path the patch also names. No format
bump: `end` is stored as found and such a `null` was always legal on read.

# Spec §11 — decisions: Transitions and motion (road map 5)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

- **R5-1 — Effects are closed vocabularies, never a runtime.** Every
  transition kind and motion preset is an enum variant or a struct the core
  range-checks, the recipe carries, the MCP catalog mirrors and the one
  compositor draws. There is no package format, no user shader, no
  expression language — which is why neither road map 5 phase adds a Metal
  pipeline.
- **R5-2 — A transition's sound is a constant-power crossfade, on by
  default for NEW transitions and absent from old files.** The overlap a
  person adds a transition at is two different moments — a Remove Silences
  cut, a jump between takes — which is uncorrelated material, where
  constant power holds the level and equal gain dips 3 dB. A version-6 file
  has no `audio` key and sounds exactly as it did; every transition the
  core mints from version 7 on says `audio: true, curve: ease_in_out`. One
  constructor, `Transition::minted`, is the only place those two values are
  written.
- **R5-3 — `add_transition` builds the overlap from handles, clamps the
  duration, and never moves a third clip.** A shorter transition is the
  same edit at a size the media allows; a gap closed part-way
  (`close_gap`'s refusal) is a different edit. Not being at a hard cut is a
  wrong ARGUMENT (`Err`), because the op is pointed at one cut by a caller
  who meant that cut — unlike `roll`, which a drag can reach at any edge;
  having no handle is a domain refusal (`Outcome::Refused`, §5.5 — it
  says so in its own sentence since road map 7's D2·3).
  **Amended 2026-09-16, by the user: when there is no handle, OFFER to
  shift.** Two whole files placed back to back — the most common screencast
  cut — have no handle on either side, so the rule above left Clip ▸
  Transition ▸ with nothing to do but refuse. `add_transition` gained
  `ripple`, and the refusal sheet a button that sends it: the incoming clip
  and everything at or after the cut on every unlocked track slide left, the
  timeline gets shorter, and the tracks stay in sync (the user chose
  "everything after", over "the rest of this track" and "just the clip").
  The rule above still holds for the default form, which is still what the
  menu tries first: a third clip moves only when a person has been told it
  will and said yes, or an agent passed `ripple` by name.
- **R5-4 — Motion is a presentation term.** `video.motion` is stored in the
  model and drawn by the recipe, but `evaluate_clip`, `get_project`, the
  inspector's fields and every edit read the clip un-moved. It is the
  second place the recipe draws what the model does not say — the first
  being the forced `normal` blend under a transition (§7.3). It is not an
  animation target: an action cannot animate it, and a file that tries is
  drawn with the base motion.
- **R5-5 — Motion is a pure function of clip time.** No seed, no wall
  clock, no previous frame: `render_frame` at a tick is byte-identical run
  after run, preview and export agree, and two clips with the same preset
  at the same clip time are displaced identically.
- **E2-27 — A zero-duration edge is configured but inactive.** Zero stays
  legal and stored for In and Out, as D7-3 requires. The timeline draws no
  wedge for it. The inspector keeps its kind selected and its actual zero
  duration editable, while its summary and a selection-aware note disclose
  inactivity. Clip ▸ Motion keeps the stored kind checked and annotates its
  title when all or some matching selected edges are inactive. Increasing
  Duration reactivates that same preset; None or Reset removes it. Choosing
  another kind preserves the stored duration, including zero; an absent slot
  still starts at the existing 0.5 s default. This is presentation only:
  the core's render-time motion contract and R5-4/R5-5 do not change.
- **G-1 — A graphic is a SOURCE, not an effect; R5-1 stands for effects**
  (road map 10 §4, 2026-09-25). §1 lists "a plugin system" as a non-goal,
  and R5-1 says effects are "closed vocabularies, never a runtime… no
  expression language". A graphic changes neither rule for what they
  govern: a transition, a motion preset, a filter and a blend stay closed
  vocabularies the one compositor draws, and a script cannot reach another
  clip's pixels, the timeline, the model or the editor. A graphic is a
  clip's CONTENT, in the same place a media file or an image sits — closer
  to "the user can import any PNG" than to a plugin. §1's non-goal gains one
  clause: "a clip may draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package
  (road map 10); nothing else is scriptable". The user asked for this
  reversal, as road map 3 reversed screen recording.
- **G-2 — The engine is a separate Rust crate; the core crate keeps its two
  rules** (road map 10 §4, 2026-09-25). QuickJS and resvg live in
  `graphic/`, a crate at the repo root. `framejob-core` depends on it by
  path, and ONE file, `core/src/ffi_graphic.rs`, calls into it; no module of
  the model, the ops, the plan or the recipe imports it. `core/src/` keeps
  "no pixel work" and "no filesystem" exactly; the `graphic` crate does
  pixel work and still no filesystem — the app reads every byte and hands it
  over. §7's first sentence becomes: "All pixel and sample work happens on
  the platform, except a graphic's rasterization, which is the `graphic`
  crate's (G-2)." Not JavaScriptCore and a platform rasterizer, because
  `measureText` has to be the rasterizer's own measurement or wrapped text
  overflows by a pixel (macOS has no public SVG rasterizer), because QuickJS
  gives public memory and time limits where JavaScriptCore's execution time

## Bet 6 — Camera cutout without a green screen, and camera layouts

Prefix CO. Phases CO0…CO10. Phase COn owns decisions CO-n0…CO-n9 (CO0 owns CO-1…CO-9). Spikes
CO-S1…CO-S4. Manual checks JOB-60…JOB-66 (numbers provisional; the integrator renumbers). Format
bumps are written "format N (provisional)": RC_FORMAT_VERSION is 37 at `d0661e5d`
(`core/src/format.rs:18`), and each bump is renumbered when its phase lands. Handoff directories are
`~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-co0` … `cj-co10`.

### Goal

A creator who records themselves gets three things on the camera clip that today need a green
screen or another app.

- **Remove Background.** One checkbox on a camera clip cuts the person out of their room. The
  segmentation runs on the Mac through Apple's Vision framework, in the background, and is cached
  in the package the way a reversed clip is. The edge can be shrunk, grown and softened. The drop
  shadow follows the person's outline. The camera keeps everything else Frame Job gives a clip:
  grading, LUTs, Camera Log, HDR, actions.
- **Text Behind Subject.** A title sits between the person and their background: the person's
  head passes in front of the words. It works over the camera's own room and over a screen
  recording behind a cut-out camera.
- **Camera layouts.** Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ and a Layout pop-up switch the camera at the playhead,
  with an eased move, between a corner picture (square, rounded or a circle), side by side,
  stacked for a vertical canvas, camera full and screen only. Each switch is an ordinary action on
  the camera clip and the screen clip, which the creator can drag, retime or delete on the action
  lane. The recorder offers the same layout at record time, and can land the camera with its
  background removed.
- **Hide the camera while silent.** The camera fades out while the microphone is silent and back

### Spikes

Each runs in CO0, from a shell, on the owner's Mac on AC power (`pmset` first), its rule recorded
in CO-9 before the run and its verdict in CO0's record. Instruments land under
`tools/proof/cutout_spike/`, next to the E9 instruments they extend.

- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate.**
  Question: which Vision request and rate give the best outline per second of analysis on real
  talking-head footage, and does a portrait (rotated) source need its orientation passed to Vision?
  Candidates: person `.balanced`, person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with
  `generateScaledMaskForImage`. Each at every frame and at 10 masks per second of source (nearest
  mask). Measured on S-CO4's keyed composites (ground truth below):
  J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5;
  B = mean |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge, at 1080p;
  B on the gesture segment;
  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment;
  masks per second at 1080p and 4K, pinned to the ANE.
  Also: S-CO3's portrait clip with and without `orientation:` passed, and the first Vision call of
  a fresh process (the E9 compile cost, recorded with no rule).
  **Rule.**
  (a) A candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is out.
  (b) The rate is every frame, capped at 30 masks per second of source, unless B on the gesture
  segment at 10 per second is within 5 % of B at every frame. Then 10 per second.
  (c) **Standard** is the fastest remaining candidate that runs at least 1.0× realtime at 1080p30
  at that rate and whose J is within 0.02 of the best J.
  (d) **Best** is the candidate with the lowest B, kept only if its B is at least 15 % below
  Standard's and it runs at least 0.25× realtime. Otherwise there is no Best, and no Quality
  control is built.
  (e) Orientation is passed to Vision when that raises J on the portrait clip, and the mask is
  turned back to coded orientation before it is stored.
  If S-CO4 has not arrived by CO0, (c) runs on the E9 fixtures for speed alone, Standard is person
  `.balanced` at every frame (E9's verdict), and (b), (d) and (e) run when the sample arrives,
  before CO4.

- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.**
  Question: does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact
  enough, small enough and cheap enough to play?
  Fixture: a synthetic movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and a mask movie
  written from it with the same presentation times. The bar code reads back which mask frame the
  compositor received for which picture frame.
  Encodings tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy.
  **Rule.** The mask track (CO-3) is kept when all four hold:
  (1) **Registration.** 100 % of frames show the mask of their own source frame, across a trim, ×0.5
  and ×2, a speed ramp, a freeze frame, a reversed clip, a split, a clip inside a nest, a
  cross-dissolve, and S-CO3's variable-frame-rate iPhone file.
  (2) **Round trip.** The value the fragment stage reads differs from the written byte by at most
  2/255 at every pixel, in an SDR project and in an HLG project.
  (3) **Size.** At most 15 MB per minute of 30 fps source at Standard.
  (4) **Playback.** `play_preview` of a 1080p30 camera with the mask track over a 4K screen composes
  at least 99 % of the frames it composes without it.
  Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured on (1), (2) and (4) and kept if it passes. If
  neither passes, CO stops after CO1 and the owner is asked. The chunk length is the longest of 2,
  5 and 10 s whose one-chunk reanalysis after a 1 s trim extension finishes within 3 s.

- **CO-S3 — Whether the edge needs refinement, and which.**
  Question: how much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512×384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and
  4K, and what does it cost per frame?
  Candidates:
  r0, bilinear sampling and a smoothstep remap (the edge and feather controls);
  r1, a joint bilateral upsample inside the layer stage (3×3 mask texels weighted by the picture's
  colour distance, read as `KeyReading` reads);
  r2, a guided filter in a pass before the destination, at twice the mask's size.
  Measured: B (as in S1) on S-CO4's composites, and cost per frame, full-frame, at 1080p and 4K
  (200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of medians — MT0's method).
  **Rule.** The cheapest candidate whose B is at most 1.1 × the lowest B ships, provided it costs at
  most 1.0 ms at 1080p and 3.0 ms at 4K above r0. If r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0 ships
  and the better one is filed with its numbers.

- **CO-S4 — The analysis beside playback.**
  Question: does analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames?
  Measured: `play_preview` of a 1080p30 project for 20 s with the analysis idle, then running.

### Goal

A creator who records themselves gets three things on the camera clip that today need a green
screen or another app.

- **Remove Background.** One checkbox on a camera clip cuts the person out of their room. The
  segmentation runs on the Mac through Apple's Vision framework, in the background, and is cached
  in the package the way a reversed clip is. The edge can be shrunk, grown and softened. The drop
  shadow follows the person's outline. The camera keeps everything else Frame Job gives a clip:
  grading, LUTs, Camera Log, HDR, actions.
- **Text Behind Subject.** A title sits between the person and their background: the person's
  head passes in front of the words. It works over the camera's own room and over a screen
  recording behind a cut-out camera.
- **Camera layouts.** Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ and a Layout pop-up switch the camera at the playhead,
  with an eased move, between a corner picture (square, rounded or a circle), side by side,
  stacked for a vertical canvas, camera full and screen only. Each switch is an ordinary action on
  the camera clip and the screen clip, which the creator can drag, retime or delete on the action
  lane. The recorder offers the same layout at record time, and can land the camera with its
  background removed.
- **Hide the camera while silent.** The camera fades out while the microphone is silent and back
  in before speech resumes, read from the speech spans Frame Job already detects on the Mac.

type" is a sentence an agent can carry out.

  aspect in it, `circle` fits a square crop in it with the radius half its side. A layout writes x,
  y, scale, crop, corner radius and opacity on each role and nothing else; rotation, shadow, grade
  and cutout are the clip's own. Every number is in `core/src/layout.rs`.
- **CO-61 — A switch is an action, and it holds across later clips.** `switch_layout` writes one
  action per role, starting at `at`, of `duration` (0.5 s, `ease_in_out` by default, at least one
  frame), on the clip of that role under `at`. At a clip's first frame it writes the base props
  instead. It then writes the same placement as BASE props on each later clip of that role's track,
  up to the first later clip that carries a placement action (an action whose end names x, y,
  scale, crop, corner radius or opacity), so a switch made after cutting holds until the next
  switch. One op, one undo step, "Camera Layout".
- **CO-62 — A switch never fights a zoom.** A role clip in the switch's reach that carries a
  placement action of its own (a screencast zoom, a punch-in) is refused by name: "The screen clip
  at 1:02 zooms; nest the screen's clips so the layout moves the nest and the zoom stays inside
  it." `switch_layout {nest: true}` nests each such role's run of clips first, in the same step —
  R5-3's `ripple` precedent: a structural change happens only when a person was told and said yes,
  or an agent named it.

  camera's source pixels, the Q frame of `edit_zoom.rs`); the app passes the mean centroid of the

### Spikes

Each runs in CO0, from a shell, on the owner's Mac on AC power (`pmset` first), its rule recorded
in CO-9 before the run and its verdict in CO0's record. Instruments land under
`tools/proof/cutout_spike/`, next to the E9 instruments they extend.

- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate.**
  Question: which Vision request and rate give the best outline per second of analysis on real
  talking-head footage, and does a portrait (rotated) source need its orientation passed to Vision?
  Candidates: person `.balanced`, person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with
  `generateScaledMaskForImage`. Each at every frame and at 10 masks per second of source (nearest
  mask). Measured on S-CO4's keyed composites (ground truth below):
  J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5;
  B = mean |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge, at 1080p;
  B on the gesture segment;
  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment;
  masks per second at 1080p and 4K, pinned to the ANE.
  Also: S-CO3's portrait clip with and without `orientation:` passed, and the first Vision call of
  a fresh process (the E9 compile cost, recorded with no rule).
  **Rule.**
  (a) A candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is out.
  (b) The rate is every frame, capped at 30 masks per second of source, unless B on the gesture
  segment at 10 per second is within 5 % of B at every frame. Then 10 per second.
  (c) **Standard** is the fastest remaining candidate that runs at least 1.0× realtime at 1080p30
  at that rate and whose J is within 0.02 of the best J.
  (d) **Best** is the candidate with the lowest B, kept only if its B is at least 15 % below
  Standard's and it runs at least 0.25× realtime. Otherwise there is no Best, and no Quality
  control is built.
  (e) Orientation is passed to Vision when that raises J on the portrait clip, and the mask is
  turned back to coded orientation before it is stored.
  If S-CO4 has not arrived by CO0, (c) runs on the E9 fixtures for speed alone, Standard is person
  `.balanced` at every frame (E9's verdict), and (b), (d) and (e) run when the sample arrives,
  before CO4.

- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.**
  Question: does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact
  enough, small enough and cheap enough to play?
  Fixture: a synthetic movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and a mask movie
  written from it with the same presentation times. The bar code reads back which mask frame the
  compositor received for which picture frame.
  Encodings tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy.
  **Rule.** The mask track (CO-3) is kept when all four hold:
  (1) **Registration.** 100 % of frames show the mask of their own source frame, across a trim, ×0.5
  and ×2, a speed ramp, a freeze frame, a reversed clip, a split, a clip inside a nest, a
  cross-dissolve, and S-CO3's variable-frame-rate iPhone file.
  (2) **Round trip.** The value the fragment stage reads differs from the written byte by at most
  2/255 at every pixel, in an SDR project and in an HLG project.
  (3) **Size.** At most 15 MB per minute of 30 fps source at Standard.
  (4) **Playback.** `play_preview` of a 1080p30 camera with the mask track over a 4K screen composes
  at least 99 % of the frames it composes without it.
  Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured on (1), (2) and (4) and kept if it passes. If
  neither passes, CO stops after CO1 and the owner is asked. The chunk length is the longest of 2,
  5 and 10 s whose one-chunk reanalysis after a 1 s trim extension finishes within 3 s.

- **CO-S3 — Whether the edge needs refinement, and which.**
  Question: how much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512×384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and
  4K, and what does it cost per frame?
  Candidates:
  r0, bilinear sampling and a smoothstep remap (the edge and feather controls);
  r1, a joint bilateral upsample inside the layer stage (3×3 mask texels weighted by the picture's
  colour distance, read as `KeyReading` reads);
  r2, a guided filter in a pass before the destination, at twice the mask's size.
  Measured: B (as in S1) on S-CO4's composites, and cost per frame, full-frame, at 1080p and 4K
  (200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of medians — MT0's method).
  **Rule.** The cheapest candidate whose B is at most 1.1 × the lowest B ships, provided it costs at
  most 1.0 ms at 1080p and 3.0 ms at 4K above r0. If r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0 ships
  and the better one is filed with its numbers.

- **CO-S4 — The analysis beside playback.**
  Question: does analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames?
  Measured: `play_preview` of a 1080p30 project for 20 s with the analysis idle, then running.
  **Rule.** If composed frames fall by more than 2 %, the analysis pauses while any transport plays
  (`BackgroundRender`'s transports) and resumes when none does. Otherwise it runs throughout.

  {behind_subject: true}`, and, when the clip has no cutout, `set_video {cutout: {background:
  keep}}` — one step, "Text Behind Subject"); the checkbox row.
- **MCP:** `set_video`'s description names `behind_subject`; `add_text_clip`'s catalog comment
  names Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject as composed of `add_track`, `add_text_clip` and `set_video`.
- **Docs:** spec §5.2a, §7.3 (subject copies; the third override), `docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md`,
  `menus-and-shortcuts.md`, `designs/spec/11-decisions/mattes.md` amendments.
- **Decisions:** CO-50…CO-53; MT-1, MT-2, MT-4 amended.
- **Acceptance:** proof rows; `make gate`.
- **Proof (`co5_proof.py`, Release, with the bar-code stand-in and a real person fixture):**
  - B1: where the subject's mask is 255, the behind title's pixels are absent (the frame equals the
    title hidden); where 0, present.
  - B2: a title in FRONT of the camera's track with the flag set is cut only by subjects behind
    it, so a camera on a higher track does not cut it.
  - B3: a split, a move and an undo of the camera keep the cut (no stored link).
  - B4: `background: keep` draws the camera whole and still cuts the title.
  - B5: the title's drop shadow is cut with it.
  - B6: a frame with no behind clip lists no subject group (the recipe is what it was).
- **Mutants:** subjects taken from tracks in front (B2); the copy drawn with the camera's shadow
  (MT-4's override dropped; B5); the group listed without a cut layer (B6).
- **Manual checks:** **JOB-62** — on S-CO1, a title behind the owner: no visible halo or gap where
  the soft edge meets the letters.
- **Depends on:** CO2, CO3; CO4 for its final look.
- **Questions for the owner:** a clip flag or a track flag ("Track ▸ Behind Subject").
  *Recommended: a clip flag, because a title is placed per moment and a track flag would catch
  every later clip on that track.*

#### CO6 — layouts at the playhead

- **What a person gets:** Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ Corner, Rounded Corner, Circle, Side by Side,
  Stacked, Camera Full and Screen Only, plus Corner ▸ the four corners. With two video clips
  selected, the front one is the camera and the one behind it the screen. With one selected, it is
  the camera, and the screen is the front-most clip drawing behind it at the playhead. With none
  selected, the camera is the clip at the playhead on the front-most track named "Camera". The
  switch eases over half a second from the playhead and holds until the next switch.
- **Core:**
  - `layout.rs` (new): CO-60's geometry, pure — each layout's target x, y, scale, crop, radius and
    opacity for a camera of `sw × sh`, a screen of its size and the container's canvas, through
    (★) and `edit_fit.rs`. `core/tests/layout.rs` checks each layout's boxes on 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1
    canvases, and that `corner`/`square` equals CAM-10 (3)'s numbers exactly.
  - `edit_layout.rs` (new): `switch_layout {camera, screen?, layout, shape?, corner?, at,
    duration?, curve?, focus?, nest?}`, composing `add_action`, `set_action_end`, `set_video` and,
    with `nest`, `nest` — CO-61's propagation and CO-62's refusals.
  - The op table row in `op_table.rs` and `edit.rs`.
- **FFI:** none.
- **Swift:** `ReelOps.swift`'s builder; `AppDelegate+ClipMenus.swift`'s submenu;
  `EditorViewController+Layout.swift` (the role rule above, the refusal beep through the refusal
  strip).
- **MCP:** `switch_layout` as an op tool (its arguments printed from the core's schema), with a
  catalog row naming Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ and `scope` declared. Tool count +1.
- **Docs:** spec §6 (`switch_layout`), §9, `docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md` (Camera layouts),
  `menus-and-shortcuts.md`.
- **Decisions:** CO-60…CO-62.
- **Acceptance:** core tests; proof rows; `make gate`.
- **Proof (`co6_proof.py`, Release, read back through `get_project` and `render_frame`):**
  - L1: each layout lands its action's end at the core's numbers on a 1920×1080 and a 1080×1920
    canvas.
  - L2: a switch at a clip's first frame writes base props and no action.
  - L3: after three cuts, a switch at the second clip carries to the third and fourth, and stops at
    a fifth that holds an earlier switch's action.
  - L4: a screen with a zoom action is refused in its own sentence; `nest: true` nests it, switches,
    and the zoom still fills the nested box (frame compare).
  - L5: one undo restores the project byte for byte.
  - L6: Circle's crop is square and its radius half the side; Rounded's radius is the documented
    fraction.
  - L7: the camera clip at the playhead inside an existing action is refused naming that action.
- **Mutants:** propagation stopping at the first later clip (L3); propagation running past an
  earlier switch (L3); the zoom refusal dropped (L4); circle's radius from the uncropped side (L6).
- **Manual checks:** **JOB-63** — on S-CO5, each switch's eased move reads as deliberate, not
  jumpy, at 0.5 s.
- **Depends on:** CO0 (T2 if `edit_action.rs` is touched; it is not planned to be).
- **Questions for the owner:** the default switch length (*recommended 0.5 s, ease in and out*); and
  CO-62's offer versus nesting the screen automatically on the first switch (*recommended: the
  offer, because a nest changes how every later edit of the screen works and should be seen being
  made*).

#### CO7 — the Layout pop-up, the nest offer and the crop on the person

- **What a person gets:** a **Layout** section in the camera clip's Picture sub-tab: a Layout
  pop-up, Corner and Shape pop-ups, a Duration field and Switch at Playhead. The refusal from
  CO-62 becomes a sheet with Nest and Switch / Cancel. The circle, side-by-side and stacked crops
  centre on the person when the clip has masks.
- **Core:** none beyond CO6.
- **Swift:**
  - `VideoPane+Layout.swift` (new), registered in `ClipPane.makeSections()` for a single selected
    media clip.
  - `LayoutOfferSheet.swift` (new) — after R5-3's shift sheet.
  - `MaskCache.centroid(clip:)` — the mean mask centroid over the clip's window, read from cached
    chunks only.
- **MCP:** none new (`switch_layout {nest, focus}` already exist); the catalog row names the
  section.
- **Docs:** spec §4.3b, `docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md`.
- **Decisions:** CO-70, CO-71 (the section's rows).
- **Acceptance:** proof rows; a `screens.py` screen for the section and the sheet; `make gate`.
- **Proof (`co7_proof.py`, Release; harness):** P1: Switch at Playhead sends the op the menu sends;
  P2: with masks of a person standing left of centre, the circle's crop centre is the masks'
  centroid within a pixel; P3: without masks it is the source centre; P4: the sheet's Nest and
  Switch is one undo step.
- **Mutants:** the focus read from an unfinished chunk set (P2 on a half-analysed clip);
  the sheet's two edits as two steps (P4).
- **Manual checks:** none beyond JOB-63.
- **Depends on:** CO6; CO1 for the centroid.
- **Questions for the owner:** none expected.

#### CO8 — layout and cutout at record time

- **What a person gets:** with "Record the camera too" ticked, the recorder panel shows a Layout
  pop-up (Corner, Rounded Corner, Circle, Side by Side, Camera Full) and "Remove the camera's
  background when it lands". The camera lands in that layout, and its background is removed as the
  next undo step.
- **Core:** none.
- **Swift:**
  - `RecorderPanelController+Rows.swift` (395) takes the two rows; if that would pass 400, the
    camera rows move to `RecorderPanelController+CameraRows.swift` first.
  - `RecordingLanding+Camera.swift` — `cornerPatch` replaced by one `switch_layout` at the clip's
    first frame, `screen` the segment's screen clip.
  - `RecordingCutout.swift` (new) — the follow-up after AU-68's pattern: a separate step "Remove
    Background" on the recording's camera clips.
- **MCP:** `record_screen` admits `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout` (CAM-10 (5), CAM-4 amended);
  the catalog's description names the panel rows.
- **Docs:** `docs/guide/screen-recording.md`, spec §7.9d, `camera-recording-2.md` amendments.
- **Decisions:** CO-80 (CAM-10 (3), CAM-10 (5), CAM-11 amended), CO-81 (the follow-up step).
- **Acceptance:** proof rows; the harness and `screens.py` pin the two new keys; `make gate`.
- **Proof (`co8_proof.py`, Release, through `land_recording` at both doors):** R1: the default
  landing is byte-identical to CAM-10's (the camera clip's props read back); R2: each layout lands
  as `switch_layout`'s base props; R3: the cutout box lands the camera with `video.cutout` as a
  second undo step; R4: `record_screen {camera_layout}` without `camera` is refused in CAM-4 (2)'s
  sentence; R5: the two keys persist across a relaunch.
- **Mutants:** the cutout folded into the landing's step (R3); the default layout changed (R1).
- **Manual checks:** none (landing is fully measured).
- **Depends on:** CO6; CO3 for the cutout box.
- **Questions for the owner:** the panel's default layout. *Recommended: Rounded Corner, the look
  creators expect, accepting that R1's pin moves; or Corner, which keeps today's landing.*

#### CO9 — hide the camera while silent

- **What a person gets:** a **Hide While Silent** section on a picture clip: on/off, Speech from (a
  pop-up of the audio media playing under the clip, the microphone first), Pre-roll, Hold and Fade.
  The camera fades out during pauses and back in just before speech, and the timeline draws the
  fade line on the clip, as Duck by Speech draws its line.
- **Core:**
  - `video.hide_silent` (format N, provisional) in `model_props.rs`.
  - `video_gate.rs` (new): the gate at a tick from the instances of `media` in the container,
    through `speech_in_clip`, widened and merged; its ramps for the plan's `gates`.
  - The multiply where `recipe.rs`'s `moved` runs (one call); `remove_media` clearing gates.
  - `core/tests/hide_silent.rs`.
- **Swift:**
  - `VideoPane+HideSilent.swift` (new) — the section; it writes `DuckSpeech.ops`'s
    `set_media_speech` before the `set_video` in one step, as Duck by Speech does.
  - `TimelineView+GateLine.swift` (new) — drawn after the duck line; `CompositionPlan.swift`
    decodes `gates`.
- **MCP:** `set_video`'s description names `hide_silent` and its need for `media.speech`.
- **Docs:** spec §5.2a, §7.2 (`gates`), §7.3, `docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md`, AU-110 amended.
- **Decisions:** CO-90, CO-91 (defaults: pre-roll 0.2 s, hold 1.5 s, fade 0.3 s).
- **Acceptance:** core tests; proof rows; `make gate`.
- **Proof (`co9_proof.py`, Release):** H1: on a fixture with known speech spans, the camera's
  rendered opacity is 1 inside each widened span, 0 in a gap longer than pre-roll + hold + 2 ×
  fade, and the ramp's midpoint at the documented tick; H2: a ripple delete through the
  microphone and camera keeps the gate on the speech (no stored times); H3: where no clip of the
  media plays, the camera shows; H4: `clip_state` reads opacity un-gated; H5: removing the media
  clears the gate.
- **Mutants:** pre-roll applied after the span (H1); the gate stored as times (H2); gated opacity
  leaking into `clip_state` (H4).
- **Manual checks:** **JOB-64** — on S-CO5, the camera leaves and returns at moments that feel
  natural, with no flicker on short pauses.
- **Depends on:** CO0.
- **Questions for the owner:** fade versus "Screen Only" layout on silence. *Recommended: fade, as
  the bet states; a silence-driven layout switch would write actions and fight CO-61's switches.*

- **What a person gets:** Remove Background and Behind Subject on a photo or a freeze frame; a
  photo may cut its foreground object, not only a person.
- **Core:** `CutoutSubject::Foreground` (format N, provisional), accepted on image and still clips
  only, refused on a media clip by name (CO-1).
- **Swift:** `PersonMaskAnalyzer`'s still arm (one mask per image, cached under `MaskCache`), bound
  at `texture(4)` by `LayerRenderersImage.swift`'s layer; the section's Subject pop-up for pictures.
- **MCP:** the `set_video` description.
- **Docs:** `docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md`.
- **Decisions:** CO-100.
- **Acceptance / proof (`co10_proof.py`, Release):** S1: a person still cut with `person` and a
  pencils still with `foreground` make the masked pixels the background; S2: `foreground` on a media
  clip refused; S3: a still of a cut-out video clip uses the video's mask for its frame.
- **Mutants:** `foreground` admitted on media (S2).
- **Manual checks:** **JOB-66** — a portrait photo's cutout edge on hair.
- **Depends on:** CO4.
- **Questions for the owner:** whether pictures are worth building in this road map. *Recommended:
  yes, but last, and it can be filed instead without touching CO0–CO9.*

### Samples and fixtures

The owner's cameras are a LUMIX GH5 and an iPhone 18 Pro. Each sample goes in `samples/` (with
its line in `samples/README.md`); proofs skip by name when one is absent, and no phase waits for
one except as stated.

| Sample | What to record | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| S-CO1 | GH5, standard (Rec. 709) profile, 1080p30 and 4K30, 2 min of the owner talking to camera at a desk in an ordinary room: hand gestures, a head turn, hair against a busy background | Analysis speed at both sizes (CO-S1, M9); JOB-60's edges; JOB-62 |
| S-CO2 | GH5 in V-Log, 10-bit, 30 s of the same shot | The log path through step 0 (CO-7, M4) |
| S-CO3 | iPhone 18 Pro, default settings (HLG HDR, variable frame rate), 1 min landscape and 20 s portrait | The HLG path, rotation (CO-S1 (e), M5) and a VFR file's registration (CO-S2 (1)) |
| S-CO4 | Either camera, 1080p30, the owner in front of an evenly lit green or blue cloth (or any saturated plain colour unlike skin and clothes): 15 s still, 20 s gesturing, 15 s turning the head with hair visible, 10 s leaning out of frame | Ground truth. Frame Job's own chroma key makes a reference alpha, and the keyed person composited over a screen recording, a photo under a slow pan and a dark wall gives three clips with exact truth for J and B (CO-S1, CO-S3, E1) |
| S-CO5 | A Frame Job screen recording with the camera beside the screen and the microphone, 3–5 min of a real tutorial with natural pauses | Layouts (JOB-63), hide while silent (JOB-64), text behind subject; the lead-segment video |
| S-CO6 | Optional, shared with bet 5: two people in one camera frame, 1 min | Two-person masks; instance masks if CO-S1 keeps them |

**Synthetic stand-ins** (no personal data): the E9 fixtures from `vision_fixtures.sh` (system-shipped
person stills, the slow push-in `job_person_60s.mov`, the no-person UI scroll `job_ui_60s.mov`); the
CO-S2 bar-code movie and `-RCDevMaskFixture`, which make registration exact and independent of
Vision; Apple Log and HLG fixtures generated with `ffmpeg` tags for the step-0 path until S-CO2 and
S-CO3 exist. Nothing synthetic stands in for S-CO4's ground truth: until it arrives, CO-S1 and CO-S3
run their speed halves only.

### Risks

- **Edges.** Balanced masks are 512×384 stretched over the frame; hair and fast hands may look cut
  with scissors. CO-S3 bounds what refinement buys and JOB-60 is the owner's verdict. If it is "not
  good enough", the remedy is a bundled model, which CO-1 keeps out of this road map.
- **Vision misses** backlit, from-behind and small figures (E9 §5b). The status says "No person
  found" for a window; a partial miss mid-clip shows as a missing arm.
- **Analysis time.** At every frame, Standard runs about 1× realtime: an hour of camera is about an
  hour of background work. Chunks limit it to the windows clips use, and the order follows the
  playhead.
- **Cache size.** CO-S2 bounds Standard at 15 MB per minute; Best may be several times that.
- **The mask track's colour.** An HLG composition must not colour-manage a mask frame. CO-S2 (2)
  measures it; a failure moves CO-3 to the fallback.
- **Decoders.** Each cut-out instance adds a decode. The eight-decoder warning counts them; a
  heavy project warns sooner.
- **Masks differ across Macs.** GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels. A package carries its
  masks; a Mac that regenerates them may draw a slightly different edge. Proofs compare against
  cached masks.
- **Layouts against existing placement.** A switch replaces the placement of later clips up to the
  next switch; a hand-placed camera there is overwritten. Zooms and punch-ins are refused and
  nested (CO-62), and a nested screen loses rounded corners, because a nest clip's radius reaches
  no layer (`nest.rs:382`).
- **Bet interactions.** Bet 1's cuts split every unlocked track, which CO-61's propagation
  handles. Bet 1 shows words inside a nest as not editable, and CO-62 may nest picture clips; it
  never nests the microphone. Bet 2's cursor layer must ride with the screen clip or its nest, or
  layouts will separate them. Bet 3's vertical version should use `stacked` for screen-and-camera
  pairs rather than reframing each clip.
- **API drift.** If Apple deprecates the `VN*` segmentation classes in favour of the `async`-only
  Swift API (as `NSCursor.currentSystem` was deprecated), the analyser needs the `async`
  confinement W-8 allows, in `MediaImporter.swift` or a decision that widens it.
- **Licences.** Concat, Cap and OpenScreen code, shaders and models are not opened or carried over.

### Not in this bet

- Replacing or blurring the background with something else as one command. It is already a
  composition (cutout plus Add Background or a blurred copy behind) and can be a later preset.
- Tracking or choosing one person among several, a brush to correct the mask, and rotoscoping.
- Non-person cutout on video (it flickers, E9 §5b).
- A cut-out live preview in the recorder panel, and anything that changes how the camera records.
  The system's own camera effects (Portrait, background replacement in Control Center) bake into
  the file when the creator turns them on, and Frame Job neither reads nor toggles them.
- Layouts with more than one camera or a grid of guests (bet 5's ground), a layout lane separate
  from actions, and layout shapes beyond square, rounded and circle.
- Face-tracking zoom on the camera, eye contact and retouching.
- A shipped or downloaded matting model (CO-1).

content.content:
1	## Bet 6 — Camera cutout without a green screen, and camera layouts
2	
3	Prefix CO. Phases CO0…CO10. Phase COn owns decisions CO-n0…CO-n9 (CO0 owns CO-1…CO-9). Spikes
4	CO-S1…CO-S4. Manual checks JOB-60…JOB-65 (numbers provisional; the integrator renumbers). Format
5	bumps are written "format N (provisional)": RC_FORMAT_VERSION is 37 at `d0661e5d`
6	(`core/src/format.rs:18`), and each bump is renumbered when its phase lands. Handoff directories are
7	`~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-co0` … `cj-co10`.
8	
9	### Goal
10	
11	A creator who records themselves gets three things on the camera clip that today need a green
12	screen or another app.
13	
14	- **Remove Background.** One checkbox on a camera clip cuts the person out of their room. The
15	  segmentation runs on the Mac through Apple's Vision framework, in the background, and is cached
16	  in the package the way a reversed clip is. The edge can be shrunk, grown and softened. The drop
17	  shadow follows the person's outline. The camera keeps everything else Frame Job gives a clip:
18	  grading, LUTs, Camera Log, HDR, actions.
19	- **Text Behind Subject.** A title sits between the person and their background: the person's
20	  head passes in front of the words. It works over the camera's own room and over a screen
21	  recording behind a cut-out camera.
22	- **Camera layouts.** Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ and a Layout pop-up switch the camera at the playhead,
23	  with an eased move, between a corner picture (square, rounded or a circle), side by side,
24	  stacked for a vertical canvas, camera full and screen only. Each switch is an ordinary action on
25	  the camera clip and the screen clip, which the creator can drag, retime or delete on the action
26	  lane. The recorder offers the same layout at record time, and can land the camera with its
27	  background removed.
28	- **Hide the camera while silent.** The camera fades out while the microphone is silent and back
29	  in before speech resumes, read from the speech spans Frame Job already detects on the Mac.
30	
31	Every control has an MCP mirror, so "put me in a circle bottom-left from 1:20, and hide me while I
32	type" is a sentence an agent can carry out.
33	
34	### Owner's answers applied
35	
36	The owner's answers of 2026-11-01, as the orchestrator reads them for this bet. Each is a default
37	the owner can change.
38	
39	- **"Add all: 1-6."** Bet 6 is in, as phases CO0…CO10 of road map "creator-jobs".
40	- **"Remove all explicit non-goals."** Spec §1's "heavy pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's
41	  one-pass shape" is lifted by the shared decision CJ-n. This bet relies on that lift and adds its
42	  own narrower rule (CO-1): Remove Background uses Vision on the Mac and ships no model. Shipping a
43	  matting model is now allowed, but it is not built here. It becomes a filed candidate only if the
44	  owner's verdict on Vision's edges (JOB-60) is "not good enough". Optical-flow and stabilisation
45	  stay unbuilt; nothing here needs them.
46	- **"The recorder can ask for input monitoring."** Not used by this bet. The recorder's camera
47	  rows gain a Layout pop-up and a checkbox (CO8), and neither needs a new grant.
48	- **The key rule.** Nothing in this bet needs a language model or a cloud model. Person
49	  segmentation is Vision on the Mac, which the key rule classes with Sound Analysis, Speech and
50	  Silero VAD: not "significant AI", needs no key, never disabled for want of one. Hide while silent
51	  reads Silero VAD's spans (`media.speech`, spec §11 AU-110). No control in this bet is greyed for a
52	  missing key.
53	- **"Cutting one real video per lead segment … alongside the first bet."** The owner's screen
54	  tutorial with the camera beside the screen (sample S-CO5 below) is both the lead-segment video
55	  and this bet's acceptance material. Its verdict on cutout, layouts and hide-while-silent is
56	  recorded in CO's record as JOB-60…JOB-64 results, the way grading recorded GR-9.
57	
58	### How it fits the tree
59	
60	Facts read at `d0661e5d`. Line counts are `wc -l`.
61	
62	**Nothing exists yet.** No Vision import is in `app/Sources`. `cutout` appears nowhere in
63	`core/src` or `app/Sources`. Issue #124 (Effects E9, iceboxed) holds the earlier design and the
64	proposed decision D5, which was never entered in §11. Its spike is
65	`tools/proof/effects_spike/vision_{common,stills,job}.swift` and `vision_fixtures.sh`, with the
66	measurements in `archive/effects-survey.md` §5b and `designs/adr/effects-survey.md`:
67	
68	- `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` is synchronous through `VNImageRequestHandler` and needs no
69	  grant. Masks are always 4:3 whatever the input: fast 256×192, balanced 512×384, accurate
70	  2016×1512, stretched over the frame in normalised coordinates, y down.
71	- Warm medians at 1080p: fast 6.6 ms, balanced 28.3 ms, accurate 65.1 ms. At 10 masks per second
72	  of source, balanced runs 4.2–5.5× realtime and accurate 1.6–1.7×.
73	- One device is byte-identical across runs and processes; GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels.
74	  `.fast` is stateful; balanced and accurate are not.
75	- Person coverage on UI, text and cards is 0.00 %. Foreground instance masks flip up to 57 % of
76	  pixels on a slow push-in, so they are for stills only.
77	- Not measured: real camera footage, hair, motion blur, the first-ever Neural Engine compile.
78	- The issue's `texture(2)` is stale. Its own last comment says the cutout takes `texture(4)`.
79	
80	**Availability.** `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` (macOS 12), `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest`
81	and `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (macOS 14) and `VNRequest.setComputeDevice(_:for:)`
82	(macOS 14) all exist on the minimum, macOS 26 (spec §11 W-8). The newer Swift `Vision` request
83	structs are `async`-only and are not used, because `async` is confined to `MediaImporter.swift` and
84	`SpeechEngine.swift` (W-8). The `VN*` classes are what the spike ran.
85	
86	**The compositor has one free texture slot to take.** The layer fragment function binds
87	`texture(0)` source, `texture(1)` matte coverage, `texture(2)` look lattice, `texture(3)` curves
88	strip (`app/Resources/Shaders/Compositor.metal:1902–1906`, 2811 lines). Coverage is multiplied at
89	step 7b (corner radius) and 7c (matte), `Compositor.metal:1771–1795`. `LayerUniforms` is 128 floats,
90	512 bytes (`Compositor.metal:221`); a new field adds a group of four. The shadow's silhouette pass
91	binds the same slots (`Compositor+Shadow.swift:221–230`), which is why a matte's cut already shapes
92	a shadow (MT-3). Every video source decodes to `64RGBAHalf` (`Compositor.swift:147`).
93	
94	**A layer's picture is a composition track.** The recipe's media source is `{kind: "track",
95	track_id}` (`core/src/recipe.rs:464–479`, 547 lines), chosen by `Assignment.video_of`, keyed by
96	instance path (`core/src/evaluate.rs:433–490`, 559 lines). The recipe publishes no source time.
97	`recipe_layer.rs` (158) is the one writer of a layer's twenty-six keys (`recipe_layer.rs:14`).
98	The plan warns past eight concurrent video tracks and never refuses
99	(`core/src/plan.rs:19`, 294 lines).
100	
101	**A reversed clip reads another file, chosen beside the plan.** `CompositionBuilder.build` reads
102	`ReverseSource.shared.resolution(for:)` (`CompositionBuilder.swift:120`, 546 lines), and `fill`
103	(`:324`) substitutes the reversed file per CLIP, with the segment's source range measured in the
104	reversed stream (`:291–303`). A clip with no file yet gets empty time and draws the slate. The core
105	keeps no mirror (spec §11 D4-6). `ReverseResolution` already carries the ramp, isolation and voice
106	render folders, so the export's capture and pin carry them with no change of their own.
107	
108	**Offline renders have one shape.** `RampAudioRenders.swift` (281) is a process-wide serial queue
109	with owners that want files (`want` `:57`, `wait` `:77`), renames into place inside
110	`CacheLedger.publish`, and a `settled` closure that posts `.reversedMediaDidChange` so the frozen
111	editor rebuilds (`ProjectDocument+RampAudio.swift`, 84). The export waits in
112	`Exporter.withRampAudio` (`Exporter+RampAudio.swift:23–30`), called at `Exporter.swift:263`;
113	`Exporter.swift` is 598 lines. `MediaCacheLane.swift` is a width-2 lane for AUDIO decodes
114	(`:29`, spec §11 #367). `BackgroundRender.swift` (116) knows every transport and whether one plays.
115	`MediaCacheLedger.swift` (231) is the generation, cancellation and save discipline every cache pass
116	obeys. A log or HDR media's strips are drawn through a one-clip composition and step 0
117	(`MediaImporter+ThumbnailSource.swift`), which is how an analysis can see such a file as SDR.
118	
119	**Mattes already cut one layer by another layer's picture.** `recipe_matte.rs` (219) emits each
120	layer's `matte: {into, cut}` and the frame's `mattes` groups; `Compositor+Matte.swift` (316) and
121	`MattePlan.swift` draw each group into a pooled destination-sized target and resolve each cut set
122	into one `r8Unorm` coverage at `texture(1)` (spec §11 MT-3, MT-6, MT-9). A matte group today comes
123	only from a matte TRACK (MT-1).
124	
125	**Placement and actions.** (★) in `core/src/edit_zoom.rs` (467) is the one placement rule, solved
126	there for a region; `add_zoom_action` composes `add_action` + `set_action_end` into one step.
127	`edit_fit.rs` (61) holds `fit_scale` and `fill_scale`. Actions on one clip may not overlap
128	(spec §5.4). Numbers, crops and corner radius interpolate; strings and booleans switch at the end.
129	A nest clip folds only x, y, scale, rotation, opacity and its crop as a clipping rect; its corner
130	radius and every per-pixel key reach no layer (`core/src/nest.rs:382–394`, 470).
131	
132	**The recorder's camera corner is Swift arithmetic.** `RecordingLanding+Camera.swift:35–66` (255)
133	computes CAM-10 (3)'s box (a quarter of the canvas wide, a third tall, inset 5 %) and writes one
134	`set_video {x, y, scale}`. The recorder panel has eleven `FrameJobRecording…` keys, among them
135	`FrameJobRecordingCameraBeside` (CAM-11) and `FrameJobRecordingEnhanceMicrophone` (AU-68, AU-69).
136	The dev tool `land_recording` lands fixture files through either door (AU-69).
137	
138	**Speech spans live on the media.** `media.speech` (format 29, AU-110) is written by
139	`set_media_speech` from the Silero VAD cache (`DuckSpeech.swift`); `speech_in_clip`
140	(`core/src/audio_duck_speech.rs:31`, 193) maps them into a clip's own time through reversal,

content.content:
11:A creator who records themselves gets four things on the camera clip that today need a green
  (R5-4), every edit, `clip_state`, `get_project` and the inspector read the clip un-gated; only the
  recipe and the plan's `gates` (the line the timeline draws) see it. `remove_media` clears every
  gate naming the media, as it clears a LUT look (`lut.rs`). Not animatable. Amends AU-110's list
  of readers.
- **CO-100 — Stills and images take a foreground subject** (format N, provisional).

**Amendments to existing decisions (draft text).**

- **§1** (shared, CJ-n): the ML clause is lifted. CO-1 narrows what this road map builds.
- **MT-1** gains: "A matte group can also be a clip's SUBJECT (CO-50): drawn by a copy of a cut-out
  layer, never by a track; the copy's clip still draws on the canvas. Only a track makes a clip a
  matte; a subject copy is the recipe's, not the model's."
- **MT-2** gains: "A clip with `video.behind_subject` is cut by the subjects behind it (CO-50) as
  well as by any matte in front of its track; the cuts multiply."
- **MT-4**: "the recipe's second deliberate override" becomes one of three. Draft: "A subject copy
  (CO-50) is the third: emitted with `background: remove`, `blend: normal`, `shadow: null` and
  `reflection: null` whatever the clip says." `core/CLAUDE.md`'s "TWO deliberate overrides" and
  spec §7.3 change in the same phase.
- **MT-6**'s last sentence ("The deferred E5 and E9 take the next free texture slots") is applied,
  not amended: the cutout takes `texture(4)`, recorded in CO-8.
- **CAM-10 (3)** becomes: "The camera is placed by `switch_layout` at its clip's first frame (CO-60,
  CO-80) with the layout the recorder chose; `corner`, shape `square`, bottom-right, is today's
  geometry to the pixel." Shapes `rounded` and `circle` add only a crop and a radius.
- **CAM-10 (5)** and **CAM-4**: `record_screen` admits `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout`, both
  refused without `camera`, in CAM-4 (2)'s step (3).
- **CAM-11** gains two panel controls and the panel's twelfth and thirteenth keys,
  `FrameJobRecordingCameraLayout` (String, absent = `corner_square`, today's landing) and
  `FrameJobRecordingCameraCutout` (Bool, absent = false), pinned in the harness and `screens.py`.
- **AU-110** gains: "A second reader, `video.hide_silent` (CO-90), reads a media's spans to show a
  picture while that media's speech plays."
- **AU-68**'s pattern is reused, not amended: the landing commits unchanged and "Remove the
  camera's background" follows as its own undo step (CO-81).
- **#124** is closed by CO2, its D5 recorded as CO-1, and its proof list carried into CO2's rows.

**Stand, and nothing here re-litigates them:** R5-1, G-1 (closed vocabulary; the cutout is a key,
not a runtime), R5-4, R5-5 (a mask is a function of the source frame, never of a previous one),
D4-6 (the mirror's one home), W-8 (no `async` outside its two files), #367 (the audio cache lane
keeps its width; video analysis gets its own lane), MT-9 (subject groups use the same pool), the
Concat rule and its extension to AGPL recorders (Cap): no code, shader, model or table is carried
over.

### Spikes

Each runs in CO0, from a shell, on the owner's Mac on AC power (`pmset` first), its rule recorded
in CO-9 before the run and its verdict in CO0's record. Instruments land under
`tools/proof/cutout_spike/`, next to the E9 instruments they extend.

- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate.**
  Question: which Vision request and rate give the best outline per second of analysis on real
  talking-head footage, and does a portrait (rotated) source need its orientation passed to Vision?
  Candidates: person `.balanced`, person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with

phases.title: Scope, the record, the tolls and the spikes
phases.gets: Nothing visible: CO-1..CO-9 recorded (Vision on the Mac with no shipped model, a per-layer mask rather than a matte track, the mask as a second composition track, chunked analysis cache, the per-window no-subject rule, uncut while pending with the export waiting, SDR analysis input, texture(4) and one uniform group), four pure-move tolls gated alone, and the verdicts of spikes CO-S1..CO-S4.

phases.title: Person masks on the Mac
phases.gets: Nothing visible yet: masks made by VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest (fresh request per frame, pinned device) for the source windows clips read, written as chunked mask movies under cache/masks/ with the ledger, marker and digest discipline, through a video analysis lane with owners and wants; log and HDR media analysed as SDR through step 0; a dev tool analyze_masks drives it.
questions_for_owner: Should analysis start as soon as a clip asks for it, or only after the Background render delay (G-38)? Recommended: at once, with CO-S4's pause while a transport plays, because it is the result the person is waiting to see.

phases.title: Remove Background drawn
phases.gets: A media or still clip with video.cutout draws only the person in the preview, render_frame and every export; pending chunks draw uncut; the export waits; the drop shadow follows the outline; set_video {cutout} for agents. Closes #124.
questions_for_owner: Confirm a frame whose mask is pending draws the clip uncut (CO-6). Recommended: uncut with the status saying so, because a blank camera reads as a bug.

phases.title: Remove Background in the inspector, the menu and analyze_cutout
phases.gets: A Background section in the Picture sub-tab after Chroma Key (Remove Background, Background Remove/Keep, Edge, Feather, Quality if CO-S1 kept Best, Status, Analyse Now), Clip ▸ Remove Background, and the analyze_cutout tool that reports and waits for the analysis.
questions_for_owner: A key for Clip ▸ Remove Background? Recommended: none in this phase; §9 is crowded and the checkbox is one click.

phases.title: Edges: refinement and HDR reading
phases.gets: The outline follows hair and shoulders more closely by CO-S3's chosen refinement, reading the picture as the chroma key does so an HLG project cuts the same outline as an SDR one; Best quality if CO-S1 kept it. The owner's edge verdict (JOB-60).
questions_for_owner: Should Best be the default on short clips? Recommended: Standard always, Best chosen per clip, since Best's analysis time is a cost the person should choose.

phases.title: Text Behind Subject
phases.gets: Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject places a title on a new track above the cut-out clip, behind the person; any clip can be marked Behind Subject; a camera that keeps its background still hides the title behind the person. Drawn as alpha_inverted subject groups through the existing matte machinery, a per-instant relation no edit can break.
questions_for_owner: Behind Subject as a clip flag or a track flag? Recommended: a clip flag, because a title is placed per moment and a track flag would catch every later clip on the track.

phases.title: Layout geometry and switch_layout
phases.gets: Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ Corner, Rounded Corner, Circle, Side by Side, Stacked, Camera Full, Screen Only (and the corner) switch the camera and screen at the playhead with an eased action that holds across later clips until the next switch; a screen that zooms is refused with nest named as the fix, or nested by nest: true; the switch_layout op tool.
questions_for_owner: Default switch length? Recommended: 0.5 s, ease in and out.

Offer to nest a zooming screen (CO-62), or nest it automatically on the first switch? Recommended: the offer, because a nest changes how every later edit of the screen works and should be seen being made.

phases.title: The Layout pop-up, the nest offer and the crop on the person
phases.gets: A Layout section in the camera clip's Picture sub-tab (Layout, Corner, Shape, Duration, Switch at Playhead), a Nest and Switch sheet for CO-62's refusal, and crops centred on the person from the clip's cached masks.

phases.title: Layout and cutout at record time
phases.gets: With Record the camera too ticked, the recorder panel offers a Layout pop-up and Remove the camera's background when it lands; the camera lands in that layout through switch_layout, and its background is removed as the next undo step; record_screen takes camera_layout and camera_cutout.
questions_for_owner: The panel's default layout: Rounded Corner (the look creators expect; R1's pin moves) or Corner (today's landing to the pixel)? Recommended: Rounded Corner.

phases.title: Hide the camera while silent
phases.gets: A Hide While Silent section on a picture clip (Speech from, Pre-roll, Hold, Fade): the camera fades out during the microphone's pauses and back in before speech, read from media.speech as a presentation term, with the fade line drawn on the timeline clip.
questions_for_owner: Fade the camera, or switch to Screen Only on silence? Recommended: fade, as the bet states; a silence-driven layout switch would write actions and fight CO-61's switches.
Defaults pre-roll 0.2 s, hold 1.5 s, fade 0.3 s? Recommended: yes, tuned on S-CO5 at JOB-64.

phases.title: Cutout on stills and pictures

spikes.question: Which Vision request (person balanced, person accurate, person instance mask) and which rate (every frame vs 10 per second) give the best outline per second of analysis on real talking-head footage, and does a portrait source need its orientation passed to Vision?
spikes.rule: Measured on S-CO4's keyed composites (J = IoU, B = mean error in an 8 px edge band at 1080p, flicker on the still segment, masks/s at 1080p and 4K on the ANE). (a) flicker > 2 levels is out; (b) rate is every frame capped at 30/s unless B at 10/s on the gesture segment is within 5 % of every-frame B; (c) Standard = fastest candidate >= 1.0x realtime at 1080p30 with J within 0.02 of the best; (d) Best = lowest-B candidate, kept only if B is >= 15 % below Standard's and it runs >= 0.25x realtime, else no Quality control; (e) pass orientation to Vision when it raises J on the portrait clip, store masks in coded orientation. Without S-CO4 at CO0, Standard = person balanced every frame and (b), (d), (e) run before CO4.

spikes.question: Does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact, small and cheap enough to play, and how long should a chunk be?
spikes.rule: Keep the mask track (CO-3) only if all hold: (1) 100 % of frames show their own source frame's mask (bar-code fixture) across a trim, x0.5, x2, a ramp, a freeze, a reverse, a split, a nest, a cross-dissolve and a VFR iPhone file; (2) the value read in the fragment stage is within 2/255 of the written byte at every pixel in SDR and HLG projects; (3) <= 15 MB per minute of 30 fps source at Standard; (4) play_preview of a 1080p30 camera with mask over a 4K screen composes >= 99 % of the frames it composes without it. Else measure the per-media mask pack on (1), (2), (4) and keep it if it passes; if neither, stop after CO1 and ask the owner. Chunks are 10 s, shortened to 5 s only if 5 s chunks cost under 5 % more analysis time per minute.

spikes.question: How much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512x384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and 4K, and what does it cost per frame?
spikes.rule: Candidates r0 (bilinear + smoothstep remap), r1 (joint bilateral upsample in the layer stage, guide read as KeyReading reads), r2 (guided-filter pre-pass at twice the mask size). Ship the cheapest whose B <= 1.1 x the lowest B, provided its cost above r0 is <= 1.0 ms at 1080p and <= 3.0 ms at 4K full frame (MT0's method: 200 frames, three interleaved runs, median of medians). If r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0 ships and the better one is filed with its numbers.

spikes.question: Does analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames, and what does the first Vision call of a fresh process cost?
spikes.rule: play_preview of a 1080p30 project for 20 s with analysis idle, then running: if composed frames fall by more than 2 %, the analysis pauses while any transport plays (BackgroundRender's transports) and resumes when none does; otherwise it runs throughout. The first-call cost is recorded with no rule.

risks: Edge quality: balanced masks are 512x384 stretched over the frame, so hair and fast hands may look cut with scissors; CO-S3 bounds what refinement buys and JOB-60 is the owner's verdict, after which only a bundled model (kept out by CO-1) would do better.
Vision misses backlit, from-behind and small figures (E9 §5b); a partial miss mid-clip shows as a missing arm.
Analysis time: every-frame Standard runs about 1x realtime, so an hour of camera is about an hour of background work; chunks limit it to used windows.
Cache size: CO-S2 bounds Standard at 15 MB per minute; Best may be several times that.
An HLG composition might colour-manage the mask track; CO-S2 (2) measures it and a failure moves CO-3 to the mask-pack fallback.
Each cut-out instance adds a decode, so the eight-decoder warning arrives sooner.
Masks differ across Macs (GPU vs ANE up to 25 levels); packages carry their masks and proofs compare against the cache, but a regenerated mask may draw a slightly different edge.

A layout switch overwrites the base placement of later clips up to the next switch; zooms and punch-ins are refused and must be nested, and a nested screen loses rounded corners because a nest clip's radius reaches no layer (nest.rs:382).
Interactions with bets 1, 2 and 3 (cuts splitting role clips, the cursor layer, vertical versions) need coordination or layouts separate what belongs together.
If Apple deprecates the VN* segmentation classes in favour of the async-only Swift Vision API, the analyser needs W-8's async confinement or a decision widening it.
